routes.name: UAE Golden Visa
routes.summary: 5- or 10-year renewable, self-sponsored residence for qualifying investors, entrepreneurs, exceptional talent, students and other designated categories.
routes.duration: 5 or 10 years depending on category, renewable while the category conditions continue to be met.

source.label: UAE Government Portal — Golden Visa
source.authority: UAE Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Ports Security (ICP)

routes.name: UAE Green Visa
routes.summary: 5-year self-sponsored residence for skilled employees, freelancers, and investors.
routes.duration: 5 years, renewable.

source.label: UAE Government Portal — Green residence

routes.name: UAE Employment (Standard Residence) visa
routes.summary: Standard employer-sponsored residence for workers recruited by UAE companies.
routes.duration: 2 or 3 years, tied to employer.

source.label: UAE Government Portal — Residence visas

routes.name: UAE Virtual Working Programme
routes.summary: 1-year residence for remote workers employed by companies outside the UAE.
routes.duration: 1 year, renewable.

source.label: Visit Dubai — Virtual Working Programme

routes.name: UAE Green Residence — investor / business partner
routes.summary: 5-year renewable, self-sponsored Green Residence for investors and business partners in UAE commercial activities.
routes.duration: 5 years, renewable while the investment and activity conditions remain met.

source.label: UAE Government Portal — Green visa for investors
source.authority: The Official Platform of the UAE Government

routes.name: UAE freelance permit with residence
routes.summary: Self-sponsored freelance residence via MOHRE or free-zone freelance permits.
routes.duration: 2–5 years depending on scheme.

source.label: MOHRE — Freelance permit
source.authority: Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation

routes.name: Skills in Demand visa (subclass 482)
routes.summary: Employer-sponsored temporary work visa for skilled roles an Australian employer cannot fill locally.
routes.duration: Up to 4 years; Hong Kong passport holders may be granted up to 5 years.

source.label: Department of Home Affairs — Skills in Demand visa

routes.name: Skilled Independent visa (subclass 189)
routes.summary: Points-based permanent residence visa for skilled workers without employer or state sponsorship.
routes.duration: Permanent residence.

source.label: Department of Home Affairs — Skilled Independent visa (subclass 189)

routes.name: Skilled Nominated visa (subclass 190)
routes.name_fa: اقامت دائم مهارتی با نامزدی ایالت
routes.summary: State-nominated permanent residence visa providing a 5-point SkillSelect boost.
routes.duration: Permanent residence.

source.label: Department of Home Affairs — Skilled Nominated visa (subclass 190)

routes.name: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491)
routes.summary: Provisional 5-year regional visa leading to permanent residence via subclass 191.
routes.duration: 5 years provisional, with pathway to permanent residence.

source.label: Department of Home Affairs — Skilled Work Regional (subclass 491)

routes.name: Employer Nomination Scheme (subclass 186)
routes.summary: Employer-nominated permanent residence for workers sponsored through Direct Entry, TRT, or Labour Agreement streams.
routes.duration: Permanent residence.

source.label: Department of Home Affairs — ENS (subclass 186)

routes.name: Working Holiday Maker visa (subclass 417/462)
routes.summary: Short-term work-and-travel visa for young people from participating countries.
routes.duration: 12 months per grant; up to 3 visas with qualifying specified work.

source.label: Department of Home Affairs — Working Holiday visa

routes.name: National Innovation visa (formerly Global Talent)
routes.summary: Permanent residence for globally recognised high achievers in target sectors — replacement for the former Global Talent visa.
routes.duration: Permanent residence.

source.label: Department of Home Affairs — National Innovation visa

routes.name: Australian Student visa (subclass 500)
routes.summary: Study visa for international students enrolled at CRICOS-registered institutions.
routes.duration: Programme length plus small buffer.

source.label: Department of Home Affairs — Student visa (subclass 500)

routes.name: Partner visa (subclass 820/801, 309/100)
routes.name_fa: پیوست به همسر یا شریک زندگی در استرالیا
routes.summary: Residence visa for spouses and de facto partners of Australian citizens, permanent residents, or eligible New Zealand citizens.
routes.duration: Initial provisional to permanent residence.

source.label: Department of Home Affairs — Partner visa

routes.name: Red-White-Red Card (Rot-Weiß-Rot-Karte)
routes.summary: Austria's criteria-based work and residence permit for qualified third-country workers, with category-specific 55-point, 70-point, graduate, self-employed, and start-up routes.
routes.duration: 24 months; then RWR Card Plus after at least 21 months of qualifying employment during the preceding 24 months.

source.label: migration.gv.at - Permanent immigration: Red-White-Red Card

routes.name: EU Blue Card (Austria)
routes.summary: EU-wide highly qualified worker permit — higher salary threshold than the RWR Card but offers intra-EU mobility after 12 months.
routes.duration: 2 years; renewable.

source.label: migration.gv.at — EU Blue Card

routes.name: Student Residence Permit (Aufenthaltsbewilligung Studierender)
routes.summary: Temporary residence permit for eligible non-EU students, with limited employer-sponsored work during study and a 12-month post-graduation job-search option.
routes.duration: Normally 12 months; renewable while the requirements and required study progress continue to be met.

source.label: OeAD — Residence Permit Student
source.authority: OeAD, Austria's Agency for Education and Internationalisation

routes.name: Family Reunification (Familiennachzug)
routes.summary: Residence permit for spouses and children of RWR Card, Blue Card, and permanent residents — spouses receive work rights via the RWR Card Plus.
routes.duration: 1 year initially; renewable. Spouses get RWR Card Plus (3 years).

source.label: migration.gv.at — Family reunification

routes.name: Red-White-Red Card — Startup Founder
routes.summary: Dedicated RWR Card category for innovative startup founders — business plan assessed by an expert jury, no points calculation needed.
routes.duration: 2 years; then RWR Card Plus progression.

source.label: migration.gv.at — Startup founders

routes.name: MERCOSUR Temporary Residence (by nationality)
routes.summary: Temporary residence for nationals of MERCOSUR member and associated states based on nationality alone, without needing a job offer or investment.
routes.duration: Granted for two years, renewable; defer to the official page for current terms.

source.label: DNM - MERCOSUR temporary residence by nationality

routes.name: Temporary Residence as a Migrant Worker
routes.summary: Temporary residence for foreign nationals hired under an employment relationship to carry out lawful paid work in Argentina.
routes.duration: Granted for one year, renewable; defer to the official page for current terms.

source.label: DNM - temporary residence as a migrant worker

routes.name: Rentista (Fixed-Income) Temporary Residence
routes.summary: Temporary residence for foreign nationals who support themselves with regular income from assets or other lawful external sources, not from personal work.
routes.duration: Granted for one year, renewable; defer to the official page for current terms.

source.label: DNM - temporary residence as rentista (No MERCOSUR)

routes.name: Inversionista (Investor) Temporary Residence
routes.summary: Temporary residence for foreign nationals who make a productive, commercial or service investment of interest to Argentina, with funds of lawful origin.
routes.duration: Granted for up to one year, renewable for periods of up to three years; defer to the official page for current terms.

source.label: DNM - temporary residence as inversionista (No MERCOSUR)

routes.name: Digital Nomad Transitory Residence
routes.summary: Transitory residence for foreign nationals who work remotely for employers or clients based abroad while staying in Argentina.
routes.duration: Granted for up to 180 days, renewable for the same period; defer to the official page for current terms.

source.label: DNM - digital nomad transitory residence

routes.name: Temporary Residence by Family Reunification
routes.summary: Temporary residence for the spouse, parents and children of an Argentine citizen or of a temporary or permanent resident.
routes.duration: Defer to the official page; terms depend on the relationship and the sponsor status.

source.label: DNM - temporary residence by family reunification

routes.name: Temporary Residence for Employment
routes.summary: If you have a job with an Armenian employer, this temporary residence status lets you live and work in Armenia and start building toward permanent residence.
routes.duration: Temporary status, commonly granted for one year at a time and renewable; from 1 November 2026 the system moves online with biometric cards - confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: Migration and Citizenship Service - residency application
source.authority: Migration and Citizenship Service, Ministry of Internal Affairs (Armenia)

routes.name: Temporary Residence for Business / Self-Employment
routes.summary: Temporary residence based on evidenced business activity in Armenia; registration, immigration permission and tax treatment are separate.
routes.duration: Temporary status can be granted for up to one year and renewed under the current procedure; check the filing-date rules.

source.label: Migration and Citizenship Service - residency application
source.authority: Migration and Citizenship Service, Ministry of Internal Affairs (Armenia)

routes.name: Residence for Ethnic Armenians (by descent)
routes.name_fa: اقامت ارمنستان بر پایه تبار ارمنی
routes.summary: If you are of Armenian descent, you can qualify for residence on the basis of your ancestry, with a faster path toward permanent residence and citizenship.
routes.duration: Temporary and permanent residence have different validity periods. Under the November reform, existing special status continues until its expiry; confirm the applicable status and filing procedure with MCS.

source.label: Migration and Citizenship Service - residency application
source.authority: Migration and Citizenship Service, Ministry of Internal Affairs (Armenia)

routes.name: Temporary Residence for Study (Armenia)
routes.summary: If you have been admitted to study at an Armenian institution, this temporary residence lets you live in Armenia for the length of your course.
routes.duration: Tied to your course and renewable while enrolled; biometric cards from 1 November 2026 - confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: Migration and Citizenship Service - residency application
source.authority: Migration and Citizenship Service, Ministry of Internal Affairs (Armenia)

routes.name: Temporary Residence for Family (Armenia)
routes.summary: If you have close family ties to an Armenian resident or citizen, this residence route lets you live in Armenia with them and build toward settlement.
routes.duration: Temporary status, commonly granted for one year at a time and renewable; biometric cards from 1 November 2026 - confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: Migration and Citizenship Service - residency application
source.authority: Migration and Citizenship Service, Ministry of Internal Affairs (Armenia)

routes.name: Permanent Residence (Armenia)
routes.summary: If you have held temporary residence in Armenia for the qualifying period, the five-year permanent residence card is your settlement status.
routes.duration: Five years, renewable under the current MCS procedure; this validity is not a new November benefit.

source.label: Migration and Citizenship Service - residency application
source.authority: Migration and Citizenship Service, Ministry of Internal Affairs (Armenia)

routes.name: Unique Permit (Leje Unike)
routes.summary: If you are a non-EU national working in Albania, the Unique Permit is the main route - one card combining work and residence, and it includes a remote-work sub-category.
routes.duration: Initially valid for one year and renewable each year; permanent residence follows after five continuous years - confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: e-Albania - Application for Unique Permit (Leje Unike)
source.authority: Border and Migration Police, Ministry of Interior (Albania) - Law 79/2021

routes.name: Unique Permit for Investors
routes.summary: If you invest in an Albanian business, the investor route of the Unique Permit grants you residence tied to that investment.
routes.duration: Tied to the investment and renewable; permanent residence follows after five continuous years - confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: e-Albania - Application for Unique Permit (Leje Unike)
source.authority: Border and Migration Police, Ministry of Interior (Albania) - Law 79/2021

routes.name: Residence by Real-Estate Ownership
routes.summary: If you own qualifying property in Albania, you can obtain residence on the basis of that ownership while you keep the property.
routes.duration: Renewable while you own the qualifying property; not a direct settlement route on its own - confirm current rules on the official page.

source.label: e-Albania - residence services (Border and Migration Police)
source.authority: Border and Migration Police, Ministry of Interior (Albania) - Law 79/2021

routes.name: Residence Permit for Studies (Albania)
routes.summary: If you have been admitted to study at an Albanian institution, this residence permit lets you live in Albania for the length of your course.
routes.duration: Tied to your course and renewable while enrolled - confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: e-Albania - residence services (Border and Migration Police)
source.authority: Border and Migration Police, Ministry of Interior (Albania) - Law 79/2021

routes.name: Family Reunification (Albania)
routes.summary: If a qualifying spouse or child has an Albanian sponsor with residence, this route can support family residence subject to housing, insurance, income and relationship rules.
routes.duration: For a foreign sponsor, the family permit is initially issued for one year and may be renewable; the Albanian-citizen spouse branch has its own first-year and renewal terms. Confirm the term on the official decision and current procedure.

source.label: Residence and Unique Permit procedure - Albanian Ministry of Interior
source.authority: Ministry of Interior / Border and Migration Police (Albania)

routes.name: Permanent Residence (Albania)
routes.summary: If you have lived in Albania continuously for five years, this is your settlement status - a long-validity permanent residence permit.
routes.duration: Long validity after five continuous years of lawful residence, renewable - confirm current rules on the official page.

source.label: e-Albania - residence services (Border and Migration Police)
source.authority: Border and Migration Police, Ministry of Interior (Albania) - Law 79/2021

routes.name: Antigua and Barbuda CBI - National Development Fund
routes.summary: For people who want citizenship of Antigua and Barbuda by making a one-time, non-refundable donation to the National Development Fund, rather than buying property or a business. This is the most popular route.
routes.duration: Full citizenship once the contribution is made and the application is approved; a short physical-presence step applies in the early years (see FAQ).

source.label: National Development Fund (NDF) - Antigua and Barbuda CIP
source.authority: Antigua and Barbuda Citizenship by Investment Unit

routes.name: Antigua and Barbuda CBI - Approved Real Estate
routes.summary: For people who would rather own an asset than donate: you buy into a government-approved property development in Antigua and Barbuda and, in return, you and your family can apply for citizenship.
routes.duration: Full citizenship; the qualifying property must be held for a minimum period before it can be resold under the programme.

source.label: Real Estate - Antigua and Barbuda CIP
source.authority: Antigua and Barbuda Citizenship by Investment Unit

routes.name: Antigua and Barbuda CBI - University of the West Indies Fund
routes.summary: For larger families seeking citizenship of Antigua and Barbuda: a donation route designed for bigger households that also helps fund the University of the West Indies and can include a tuition scholarship for one family member.
routes.duration: Full citizenship once the contribution is made and the application is approved; the early-years physical-presence step applies.

source.label: University of the West Indies (UWI) Fund - Antigua and Barbuda CIP
source.authority: Antigua and Barbuda Citizenship by Investment Unit

routes.name: Antigua and Barbuda CBI - Business Investment
routes.summary: For entrepreneurs who want citizenship of Antigua and Barbuda by investing in an approved business - either alone or jointly with other approved applicants in a larger venture.
routes.duration: Full citizenship once the qualifying business investment is made and the application is approved; the early-years physical-presence step applies.

source.label: Business Investment - Antigua and Barbuda CIP
source.authority: Antigua and Barbuda Citizenship by Investment Unit

routes.name: Antigua and Barbuda Work Permit
routes.summary: For people who have a job offer from an employer in Antigua and Barbuda. The work permit is employer-led and is completely separate from the citizenship-by-investment programme.
routes.duration: A temporary, employer-tied permit, typically issued for a defined period and renewable; it does not by itself lead to settlement.

source.label: Antigua and Barbuda Citizenship by Investment Unit - official site

routes.name: Work Permit and Temporary Residence Permit
routes.summary: For you if an Azerbaijani employer has offered you a job: this is the standard route into paid work, where your employer secures a work permit for you and you then hold a temporary residence permit to live in the country.
routes.duration: The work permit is tied to your employment, and the temporary residence permit is issued for a defined period (often up to a year) and renewed alongside it while you keep the job.

source.label: State Migration Service of Azerbaijan - residence and work permits for foreigners
source.authority: State Migration Service of the Republic of Azerbaijan

routes.name: Temporary Residence Permit (investment, real estate or deposit)
routes.summary: For you if you want residence in Azerbaijan through a financial commitment: a temporary residence permit can be granted on grounds such as a qualifying investment in the economy, owning real estate, or holding a fixed-term bank deposit - but please read the honesty note first.
routes.duration: A temporary residence permit issued for a defined period (often up to a year) and renewable while the qualifying basis continues; it can lead toward permanent residence after about two years.

source.label: State Migration Service of Azerbaijan - grounds for temporary and permanent residence
source.authority: State Migration Service of the Republic of Azerbaijan

routes.name: Permanent Residence Permit
routes.summary: For you if you have lived in Azerbaijan on temporary residence and want to settle for good: the permanent residence permit confirms your right to live there long term, generally available after about two years of qualifying temporary residence.
routes.duration: Confirms permanent residence; the permit is generally issued for a multi-year period (often around five years) and renewable while you keep your status.

source.label: State Migration Service of Azerbaijan - permanent residence after temporary residence
source.authority: State Migration Service of the Republic of Azerbaijan

routes.name: Temporary Residence Permit (family ties)
routes.summary: For you if you have close family in Azerbaijan: a temporary residence permit can be granted on the basis of a family relationship to an Azerbaijani citizen or a resident, letting you live in the country and, in time, move toward permanent residence.
routes.duration: A temporary residence permit issued for a defined period (often up to a year) and renewable while the family relationship and basis continue; it can lead toward permanent residence.

source.label: State Migration Service of Azerbaijan - temporary residence on family grounds
source.authority: State Migration Service of the Republic of Azerbaijan

routes.name: Temporary Residence Permit (students)
routes.summary: For you if you have a place to study in Azerbaijan: this route lets you live in the country for the length of your course, normally on a temporary residence permit linked to your enrolment.
routes.duration: Linked to the length of your course and renewable while you remain enrolled; it is a study route rather than a settlement route.

source.label: State Migration Service of Azerbaijan - residence permits, including for study
source.authority: State Migration Service of the Republic of Azerbaijan

routes.name: Residence and Work Authorisation (A.1)
routes.summary: Andorra authorisation for a newcomer to reside and work permanently and effectively while the permit is valid.
routes.duration: Initial authorisation for 1 year, then three renewals for 2 years each; after 7 years, renewals are generally issued for 10-year periods, subject to treaty exceptions.

source.label: A.1 Residence and work initial authorisation - Government of Andorra

routes.name: Self-Employed Residence and Work Authorisation (J.1)
routes.summary: Andorra route for a newcomer to reside in Andorra and carry out self-employed activity during the permit period.
routes.duration: Initial authorisation for 1 year, then three renewals for 2 years each; after 7 years, renewals are generally issued for 10-year periods, subject to treaty exceptions.

source.label: J.1 Self-employed residence and work initial authorisation - Government of Andorra

routes.name: Digital Nomad Residence (D.3)
routes.summary: Andorra residence route for remote workers whose work does not require a fixed geographic location and who use telecommunications and technology.
routes.duration: Initial residence authorisation for 2 years, first renewal for 2 years, second renewal for 3 years and later renewals generally for 10 years, subject to treaty exceptions.

source.label: D.3 Digital nomad residence - Government of Andorra

routes.name: Family Reunification Residence (B.1)
routes.summary: Andorra residence authorisation for qualifying family members joining an Andorran national or a residence-and-work permit holder who lives in Andorra.
routes.duration: Up to 10 years when reunited with an Andorran national; where reunited with a residence-and-work holder, the initial period is 1 year, then three renewals for 2 years and later renewals generally for 10 years.

source.label: B.1 Family reunification residence initial authorisation - Government of Andorra

routes.name: Study, Training, Elite Sport or Research Authorisation (F)
routes.summary: Andorra authorisation to live in the country while studying, doing training, elite sport training or scientific or similar research.
routes.duration: For studies, the authorisation follows the school-year duration; for training, high-level sport or research, it follows the duration of the approved activity.

source.label: F Study, training, elite sport or research authorisation - Government of Andorra

routes.name: Border Worker Authorisation (C.1)
routes.summary: Andorra work authorisation for a person who works in Andorra but habitually spends the night outside Andorran territory.
routes.duration: Initial authorisation for 1 year, then renewals for 3-year periods.

source.label: C.1 Border worker initial authorisation - Government of Andorra

routes.name: Tourist and Ordinary Short-Stay Visa
routes.summary: Short-stay Angola visa category for visitor, tourism and ordinary entry cases, with SME portal filing and official consular-fee references.
routes.duration: The public SME source set reviewed here does not publish a single standard stay length for all tourist or ordinary cases; confirm the allowed stay and extension position before travel.

source.label: SME legislation page - foreigner law, regulation and fee decrees
source.authority: Servico de Migracao e Estrangeiros, Angola

routes.name: Work Visa
routes.summary: Angola work-visa category for foreign nationals whose stay involves employment or a work assignment, with SME portal filing and official fee references.
routes.duration: The public source set reviewed here does not publish a standard work-visa validity period; confirm validity, renewal and extension timing through SME or the Angolan mission before filing.

source.label: SME legislation page - foreigner law, regulation and fee decrees
source.authority: Servico de Migracao e Estrangeiros, Angola

routes.name: Privileged Visa
routes.summary: Official Angola privileged-visa category appearing in migration fee decrees, usually relevant to investment or special economic cases that must be confirmed through SME.
routes.duration: The reviewed public SME pages do not publish a standard privileged-visa validity period; confirm the grant period and extension route through SME before filing.

source.label: SME legislation page - foreigner law, regulation and fee decrees
source.authority: Servico de Migracao e Estrangeiros, Angola

routes.name: Temporary Stay Visa
routes.summary: Angola temporary-stay visa category for longer but time-limited stays, with official SME legal and fee sources.
routes.duration: The reviewed public SME pages do not publish a standard validity period for all temporary-stay cases; confirm the grant period and extension position before filing.

source.label: SME legislation page - foreigner law, regulation and fee decrees
source.authority: Servico de Migracao e Estrangeiros, Angola

routes.name: Study Visa
routes.summary: Angola study-visa category for foreign students, backed by SME legal and official fee sources.
routes.duration: The reviewed public SME pages do not publish a standard study-visa duration; confirm validity and extension timing against the course length before filing.

source.label: SME legislation page - foreigner law, regulation and fee decrees
source.authority: Servico de Migracao e Estrangeiros, Angola

routes.name: Medical Treatment Visa
routes.summary: Angola medical-treatment visa category for treatment-related stays, with official fee and SME portal references.
routes.duration: The reviewed public SME pages do not publish a standard medical-treatment validity period; confirm the stay length, companion treatment and extension position before filing.

source.label: SME legislation page - foreigner law, regulation and fee decrees
source.authority: Servico de Migracao e Estrangeiros, Angola

routes.name: Residence Fixation Visa
routes.summary: Angola residence-fixation visa category for applicants whose purpose is to establish residence, subject to SME confirmation of the current basis.
routes.duration: The reviewed public source set does not publish a standard validity period for the residence-fixation visa; confirm the grant period and resident-card follow-up before filing.

source.label: SME legislation page - foreigner law, regulation and fee decrees
source.authority: Servico de Migracao e Estrangeiros, Angola

routes.name: Permanent Residence Card
routes.summary: Angola permanent resident-card fee category for people who have reached a qualifying residence basis and need SME resident-card processing.
routes.duration: The reviewed public source set does not publish a standard permanent-card validity period; confirm grant and renewal timing through SME.

source.label: Presidential Decree 21/19 - migration-act fees
source.authority: Servico de Migracao e Estrangeiros, Angola

routes.name: Paid Employment Work and Residence Permit
routes.summary: DIMAS route for a foreign national applying to work in Aruba for one Aruban employer in a specified job title.
routes.duration: Temporary residence/work permission as granted by DIMAS for the approved employer and job title.

source.label: DIMAS Aruba - Paid Employment
source.authority: Departamento di Integracion, Maneho y Admision di Stranhero (DIMAS)

routes.name: Short-term Project Permit
routes.summary: DIMAS business route for specific professionals working up to six months on an Aruba project while paid abroad.
routes.duration: Up to six months for the approved Aruba project.

source.label: DIMAS Aruba - Short-term projects
source.authority: Departamento di Integracion, Maneho y Admision di Stranhero (DIMAS)

routes.name: Student Temporary Residence Permit
routes.summary: DIMAS temporary residence route for adults studying full-time at a recognised educational institution in Aruba.
routes.duration: Temporary residence for the approved study period, as granted by DIMAS.

source.label: DIMAS Aruba - Student
source.authority: Departamento di Integracion, Maneho y Admision di Stranhero (DIMAS)

routes.name: Family Reunification / Family Formation Residence
routes.summary: DIMAS family residence route for spouses, registered partners and minor children joining or forming a family in Aruba.
routes.duration: Residence permission as granted by DIMAS for the approved family basis.

source.label: DIMAS Aruba - Family reunification / family formation
source.authority: Departamento di Integracion, Maneho y Admision di Stranhero (DIMAS)

routes.name: Investor and Shareholder Residence
routes.summary: DIMAS business residence route for qualifying investors and shareholders who may be exempt from the DPL labour market test.
routes.duration: Residence permission as granted by DIMAS for the approved investor or shareholder basis.

source.label: DIMAS Aruba - Investors and Shareholders
source.authority: Departamento di Integracion, Maneho y Admision di Stranhero (DIMAS)

routes.name: U.S. Citizen or National Entry Documents

routes.summary: American Samoa 30-day visitor-permit handling for travellers from U.S. Visa Waiver Program countries.
routes.duration: Up to 30 days as allowed by the visitor permit granted under current American Samoa rules.

source.label: American Samoa Department of Legal Affairs - Visitor Permits

routes.name: Non-U.S. 30-Day Sponsored Visitor Permit
routes.summary: American Samoa visitor-permit route for non-U.S. travellers who need local sponsorship for a short visit.
routes.duration: Up to 30 days as granted under the sponsored visitor-permit process.

source.label: American Samoa Department of Legal Affairs - Visitor Permits
source.authority: American Samoa Department of Legal Affairs

routes.summary: American Samoa employment-based residency route for foreign nationals whose right to live and work depends on an approved local petition.
routes.duration: Residency or employment-authorised status as granted by the Immigration Board, Attorney General or current petition process.

source.authority: American Samoa Department of Legal Affairs

routes.name: Family-Based Residency Petition
routes.summary: American Samoa family or sponsor-based residency petition route for spouses, dependants and other eligible family cases.

source.authority: American Samoa Department of Legal Affairs

routes.name: Permanent Resident Status
routes.summary: American Samoa permanent resident status for people who meet the statutory and board-administered residence criteria.
routes.duration: Permanent residence status if granted under American Samoa immigration law and current board procedures.

routes.name: Foreign Investor Entry Permit
routes.summary: American Samoa foreign investor entry-permit framework for qualifying investment activity.
routes.duration: Investor entry permission as granted under the statutory framework and current official process.

routes.name: Guest Worker Permit

routes.duration: Guest worker status as granted under the statutory chapter and current Immigration Board process.

routes.name: Single Entry eVisa
routes.name_fa: ورود به کشور الکترونیکی؛ یک‌بار ورود
routes.summary: Anguilla single-entry eVisa for eligible business or leisure visitors staying up to 90 consecutive days.
routes.duration: One stay of up to 90 consecutive days; the eVisa must be used within 90 days of issue.

source.label: eVisa Anguilla
source.authority: Government of Anguilla Department of Immigration

routes.name: Multiple Entry eVisa
routes.name_fa: ورود به کشور الکترونیکی؛ چندبار ورود
routes.summary: Anguilla multiple-entry eVisa for eligible business or leisure visitors making repeat stays of up to 90 days per visit.
routes.duration: Multiple entries, with stays up to 90 consecutive days per visit.

source.label: eVisa Anguilla
source.authority: Government of Anguilla Department of Immigration

routes.name: UK, US or Canada Visa or Residence Permit Entry
routes.summary: Anguilla eVisa portal note for travellers who hold a valid visa or residence permit to enter the UK, United States or Canada.
routes.duration: Short visitor entry, subject to current Anguilla border permission on arrival.

source.label: eVisa Anguilla
source.authority: Government of Anguilla Department of Immigration

routes.name: Residence by Investment
routes.summary: Anguilla residence-by-investment route with fund, real-estate, business-premises or combined investment options.
routes.duration: Permanent residence route; citizenship pathway timing depends on meeting the applicable requirements.

source.label: Select Anguilla - Residence by Investment

routes.name: High Value Resident Tax Residency
routes.summary: Anguilla High Value Resident programme for qualifying tax residents paying a fixed annual worldwide-income tax amount.
routes.duration: Ongoing residence/tax-residency status while programme conditions continue to be met.

source.label: Select Anguilla - Tax Residency

routes.name: Tourist e-Visa
routes.summary: Afghanistan single-entry tourist e-visa route through the official E-Afghans online visa portal.
routes.duration: Single entry, up to 30 days from the date of entry; validity expires 90 days from the date of issue.

source.label: Afghanistan Consulate Dubai - Applying for Visa
source.authority: Consulate General of Afghanistan in Dubai and Northern Emirates

routes.name: Afghan-Origin Entry Permit
routes.summary: Afghanistan entry-permit route for Afghans who hold passports other than Afghan passports.
routes.duration: Entry-permit handling; confirm current validity and entry conditions with the competent Afghan mission before travel.

source.label: Afghanistan Consulate Dubai - Entry Permit for Foreign Afghans
source.authority: Consulate General of Afghanistan in Dubai and Northern Emirates

routes.name: Work, Study or Residence Authority Check
routes.name_fa: بررسی شرایط کار، تحصیل یا اقامت
routes.summary: Afghanistan cautious authority-check route for work, study, residence or non-tourist cases not covered by the public tourist e-visa page.
routes.duration: Do not infer work, study or residence duration from the tourist e-visa; confirm the route and stay basis with the competent Afghan mission or authority.

source.label: E-Afghans Visa Portal - Visa Requirements

routes.name: Single Permit
routes.summary: Belgium’s combined residence and work authorisation for non-EU employees staying more than 90 days.
routes.duration: Usually tied to the employment authorisation and residence decision; renewable.

source.label: Immigration Office Belgium — Single Permit

routes.name: EU Blue Card
routes.summary: Belgian highly qualified employee route under the EU Blue Card framework.
routes.duration: Time-limited residence and work authorisation; renewable.

source.label: EU Immigration Portal — EU Blue Card in Belgium

routes.name: Professional Card for self-employment
routes.summary: Regional authorisation for non-EU nationals who want to work in Belgium as self-employed professionals.
routes.duration: Time-limited and renewable under regional rules.

source.label: Belgium.be — Self-employment

routes.name: Residence authorization for work (VITEM V)
routes.summary: Residence authorization for foreign nationals coming to Brazil to work, generally initiated by a Brazilian employer.
routes.duration: Commonly granted as a temporary residence aligned to the employment, with renewal and a pathway toward indefinite residence; confirm current terms on the official page.

source.label: Portal de Imigracao - Autorizacao de Residencia Laboral
source.authority: Ministerio da Justica e Seguranca Publica (MJSP)

routes.name: Residence authorization for investment
routes.summary: Residence authorization for foreign nationals making a qualifying investment in Brazil, including real-estate investment under CNIg Resolution 36/2018.
routes.duration: The real-estate investment authorization is initially granted for four years and is renewable for an indefinite period; confirm current terms on the official page.

source.label: Portal de Imigracao - Investimento Imobiliario (RN 36/2018)
source.authority: Ministerio da Justica e Seguranca Publica (MJSP) / CNIg

routes.name: Digital nomad residence (VITEM XIV)
routes.summary: Residence authorization and VITEM XIV temporary visa for remote workers employed by or contracting with employers outside Brazil.
routes.duration: Granted as a temporary residence for a defined period with the possibility of renewal; this route is not in itself a settlement track. Confirm current terms on the official page.

source.label: Portal de Imigracao - Guia Pratico para Nomades Digitais
source.authority: Ministerio da Justica e Seguranca Publica (MJSP) / CNIg

routes.name: Family reunion residence (VITEM XI)
routes.summary: Residence authorization for family members of Brazilian nationals or of immigrants who hold residence in Brazil, under Interministerial Ordinance 12/2018.
routes.duration: Residence is generally aligned to the sponsoring relationship and the sponsor status, with renewal and a pathway toward indefinite residence; confirm current terms on the official page.

source.label: Portal de Imigracao - Reuniao Familiar (PI 12/2018)
source.authority: Ministerio da Justica e Seguranca Publica (MJSP)

routes.name: MERCOSUR residence agreement (VITEM XIII)
routes.summary: Treaty-based residence for nationals of MERCOSUR member and associated states, with a path from temporary to indefinite residence.
routes.duration: Temporary residence is typically granted for up to two years and can be converted to indefinite residence on meeting the decree requirements; confirm current terms on the official page.

source.label: MERCOSUR residence - Ministry of Justice application guidance
source.authority: Ministerio da Justica e Seguranca Publica (MJSP)

routes.name: Residence for retirees and pensioners
routes.summary: Residence authorization for retired immigrants and recipients of a death pension who can transfer at least US$2,000 per month to Brazil, under CNIg Resolution 40/2019.
routes.duration: Initial residence is granted for up to two years and is renewable; confirm current terms on the official page.

source.label: Biblioteca Digital MJSP - Resolucao Normativa CNIg 40/2019 (aposentado e/ou pensionista)
source.authority: Ministerio da Justica e Seguranca Publica (MJSP) / CNIg

routes.name: LMRA Work Permit (employer-sponsored)
routes.summary: The standard employer-sponsored work permit for expatriates in Bahrain. A Bahraini employer applies through the Labour Market Regulatory Authority (LMRA) and the permit carries the associated residence.
routes.duration: Issued and renewed by the employer (commonly one- or two-year terms); tied to the employment relationship.

source.label: New Work Permit - LMRA

routes.name: Self-Sponsorship / Registered Worker Permit
routes.summary: A self-sponsorship work permit that lets eligible workers in Bahrain work without being tied to a single employer, administered by the LMRA through its Labour Registration Program.
routes.duration: Renewable self-sponsorship permit; confirm the current term on the official LMRA page.

source.label: Registered Worker (Labour Registration Program) - LMRA

routes.name: Golden Residency
routes.summary: Bahrain long-term renewable residence for property owners, retirees, talented individuals and long-term residents, issued by the NPRA. It is renewable residence, not permanent residence or citizenship.
routes.duration: Long-term renewable residency (renewable on a multi-year cycle); confirm the current term on the official NPRA page.

source.label: Golden Residency - NPRA

routes.name: Family / Dependant Residence Permit
routes.summary: Residence permit allowing an expatriate resident in Bahrain to sponsor a spouse, children and certain dependants, issued through the NPRA / LMRA residence services.
routes.duration: Renewable residence linked to the sponsor status; confirm the current term on the official NPRA page.

source.label: Residence Permits Services - NPRA

routes.name: Student Residence Permit
routes.summary: Residence permit for foreign students enrolled at a licensed educational institution in Bahrain, issued by the NPRA. Holders may not work.
routes.duration: Renewable for the duration of the course of study; confirm the current term on the official NPRA page.

source.label: Student Residence Permit - NPRA

routes.name: Barbados Work Permit
routes.summary: If a Barbadian employer wants to hire you, this is the permit that lets you work for them legally. It is employer-tied, so it starts with a job offer, not a personal application.
routes.duration: Issued short-term or long-term and tied to a specific employer and role; renewable while the job continues. Confirm the current validity bands on the official page.

source.label: Work Permits - Barbados Immigration Department

routes.name: 12-Month Barbados Welcome Stamp
routes.summary: If you work remotely for an employer or clients outside Barbados, the Welcome Stamp lets you base yourself on the island for up to a year while you keep doing that job.
routes.duration: Up to 12 months, with the option to reapply; it is a temporary remote-work visa and does not lead to permanent residence. Confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: Barbados Welcome Stamp - Official
source.authority: Government of Barbados (Welcome Stamp / Barbados Tourism Marketing Inc.)

routes.name: Barbados Immigrant Status
routes.summary: If you want to settle in Barbados long term, immigrant status is the route that gives you the right to live there on a lasting basis, usually after qualifying residence or through a close Barbadian connection.
routes.duration: A long-term, settled status once granted; subject to the conditions the Immigration Department attaches. Confirm current validity and conditions on the official page.

source.label: Immigrant Status - Barbados Immigration Department

routes.name: Special Entry and Reside Permit (SERP)
routes.summary: If you are a high-net-worth individual who wants the right to live in Barbados, the Special Entry and Reside Permit (SERP) is the long-stay permit built around significant means or investment in the island.
routes.duration: Long-stay, with validity that varies by category (some categories are granted on an indefinite basis); confirm the current terms for your category on the official page.

source.label: Special Entry Permits - Barbados Immigration Department

routes.name: Bahamas Work Permit
routes.summary: If a Bahamian employer wants to hire you, this is the permit that lets you work for them. The employer applies, usually after first advertising the role locally.
routes.duration: Issued as short-term or annual permits tied to a specific employer and post; renewable while the job continues. Confirm the current bands on the official page.

source.label: Work Permit (Work Visa) - Bahamas Department of Immigration
source.authority: Commonwealth of The Bahamas Department of Immigration

routes.name: Bahamas Economic Permanent Residence
routes.summary: If you can invest substantially in The Bahamas - typically in real estate - economic permanent residence gives you the right to live there permanently, without the right to work.
routes.duration: Permanent residence once granted, conditional on maintaining the qualifying investment for the required period; confirm current conditions on the official page.

source.label: Permanent Residence - Bahamas Department of Immigration
source.authority: Commonwealth of The Bahamas Department of Immigration

routes.name: Bahamas Extended Access Travel Stay (BEATS)
routes.summary: If you work or study remotely, BEATS is the permit that lets you do it from any of the Bahamian islands for up to a year - without taking a local job.
routes.duration: Up to one year, renewable; this is a temporary remote-work permit and does not lead to permanent residence. Confirm current validity and renewal on the official page.

source.label: BEATS - Bahamas Extended Access Travel Stay (Department of Immigration)
source.authority: Commonwealth of The Bahamas Department of Immigration

routes.name: Bahamas Annual Residence Permit
routes.summary: If you want to live in The Bahamas without working there - for example as a retiree or person of means - the annual residence permit lets you reside for a year at a time, renewably.
routes.duration: Granted for a year at a time and renewable; it is a non-working residence permit and does not by itself lead to permanent residence. Confirm current terms on the official page.

source.label: Permit To Reside - Bahamas Department of Immigration
source.authority: Commonwealth of The Bahamas Department of Immigration

routes.name: Bahamas Homeowner Residence Card
routes.summary: If you own a home in The Bahamas, the homeowner residence card gives you and your immediate family a smoother right to come and go and reside while you keep that property.
routes.duration: Valid while the qualifying property is owned and the card is kept current; it is tied to home ownership and does not by itself lead to permanent residence. Confirm current terms on the official page.

source.label: Home Owner Identification - Bahamas Department of Immigration
source.authority: Commonwealth of The Bahamas Department of Immigration

routes.name: Single Permit for Residence and Work
routes.summary: If you are a non-EU national with a Bulgarian job offer, this is the main route - one document that lets you both live and work in Bulgaria.
routes.duration: Usually granted for one to three years and renewable while you keep the qualifying job - confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: Migration Directorate - residence of foreigners

routes.name: EU Blue Card (Bulgaria)
routes.summary: If you are a highly-qualified non-EU professional with a Bulgarian job offer above the salary threshold, the EU Blue Card gives you residence plus EU-wide mobility benefits.
routes.duration: Issued for a fixed validity tied to your contract and renewable; confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: Migration Directorate - residence of foreigners

routes.name: Continuous (Long-Term) Residence Permit
routes.summary: If you have a long-stay (type D) visa and a qualifying ground to live in Bulgaria, this annually-renewable permit is the residence card you build your settlement on.
routes.duration: Generally up to one year at a time and renewable each year while your qualifying ground continues - confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: Migration Directorate - residence of foreigners

routes.name: Residence by Investment
routes.summary: If you can make a qualifying investment in Bulgaria, this route grants residence and, depending on the amount, a faster path to permanent residence.
routes.duration: A continuous residence card is generally issued first and can convert to permanent residence at higher tiers; confirm current rules on the official page.

source.label: Migration Directorate - residence of foreigners

routes.name: Residence Permit for Study (Bulgaria)
routes.summary: If you have been admitted to a Bulgarian university or college, this residence permit lets you live in Bulgaria for the length of your studies.
routes.duration: Tied to your course and renewable while you remain enrolled - confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: Migration Directorate - residence of foreigners

routes.name: Family Reunification Residence (Bulgaria)
routes.summary: If a close family member already lives lawfully in Bulgaria, this route lets you join them and build toward settlement together.
routes.duration: Generally aligned to the sponsor's permit and renewable - confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: Migration Directorate - residence of foreigners

routes.name: Permanent Residence (Bulgaria)
routes.summary: If you have lived in Bulgaria continuously for five years, this is your settlement status - secure residence and a stepping stone toward citizenship.
routes.duration: Indefinite status, subject to conditions on continued residence - confirm current rules on the official page.

source.label: Migration Directorate - residence of foreigners

routes.name: Work Permit
routes.summary: For non-citizens taking up employment in Botswana: the work permit gives you permission to work for a Botswana employer, applied for through the Department of Immigration and Citizenship on the national portal gov.bw.
routes.duration: Issued for a fixed period tied to the employment and renewable; confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: Work Permit Application - Government of Botswana

routes.name: Investor Work Permit
routes.summary: For non-citizens investing in a business in Botswana: the investor category of the work permit lets you reside and run or invest in a Botswana business, applied for through the Department of Immigration and Citizenship on gov.bw.
routes.duration: Issued for a fixed period tied to the investment and renewable; confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: Work Permit Application - Government of Botswana

routes.name: Residence Permit
routes.summary: For non-citizens who want to live in Botswana beyond a visit: the residence permit is the general permit that lets immigrants, and certain other categories, reside in the country, applied for through the Department of Immigration and Citizenship on gov.bw.
routes.duration: A renewable permit issued for a set period that depends on the category; confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: Residence Permit Application - Government of Botswana

routes.name: Residence Permit - Spouse of a Botswana Citizen
routes.summary: For the foreign husband or wife of a Botswana citizen: this category of the residence permit lets you live in Botswana on the basis of your marriage, and it can place you on the path toward longer-term settlement.
routes.duration: A renewable residence permit tied to the marriage that can support longer-term settlement; confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: Residence Permit Application - Government of Botswana

routes.name: Residence Permit - Dependants
routes.summary: For dependent family members of someone living in Botswana: this category of the residence permit lets dependants, including younger adults (18-25) and older relatives (65+), reside on the basis of their sponsor, applied for through the Department of Immigration and Citizenship.
routes.duration: A renewable residence permit tied to the dependency and the sponsor's status; confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: Residence Permit Application - Government of Botswana

routes.name: Permanent Residence
routes.summary: For non-citizens with a long, lawful stay in Botswana: permanent residence is the discretionary, durable status you can apply for after years in the country, going beyond the renewable work and residence permits.
routes.duration: Durable, long-term residence beyond the renewable permits, granted at the authorities' discretion; confirm the current validity and qualifying period on the official page.

source.label: Permanent Residence Application - Government of Botswana

routes.name: Work Pass (employer-sponsored employment)
routes.summary: For you if a Brunei employer has offered you a job: the Work Pass is the standard, employer-sponsored route into paid employment, handled by the immigration department's Foreign Work Pass division alongside a valid visa.
routes.duration: Issued for a defined, employer-tied period (often up to a couple of years) and renewable while you keep the job; it is not a settlement route.

source.label: Immigration and National Registration Department of Brunei - Work Pass
source.authority: Immigration and National Registration Department, Ministry of Home Affairs (Brunei Darussalam)

routes.name: Long-Term Pass (social, business or professional)
routes.summary: For you if you want a multi-year basis to stay in Brunei: the Long-Term Pass is a newer route with social, business and professional sub-categories - but please read the dated note, because it only took effect at the end of 2024.
routes.duration: A multi-year pass (reported as up to several years) with multiple entry; it is a long-stay route rather than a settlement status.

source.label: Immigration and National Registration Department of Brunei - Long Term Pass
source.authority: Immigration and National Registration Department, Ministry of Home Affairs (Brunei Darussalam)

routes.name: Entry Permit (route toward permanent resident status)
routes.summary: For you if you are working toward settling in Brunei: the Entry Permit is the document the immigration department processes for permanent resident status, so this is the formal route toward becoming a permanent resident.
routes.duration: The route toward permanent resident status; once granted, permanent residence is a settled status with re-entry permits issued and renewed under the rules.

source.label: Immigration and National Registration Department of Brunei - Entry Permit (Permit Masuk)
source.authority: Immigration and National Registration Department, Ministry of Home Affairs (Brunei Darussalam)

routes.name: Permanent Residence (discretionary, long-term)
routes.summary: For you if you intend to settle in Brunei for life: permanent residence confirms a long-term right to live there - but please read the honesty note, because it is discretionary and the official categories set qualifying periods of up to twenty years of residence or marriage.
routes.duration: A long-term settled status; the official categories set qualifying periods of up to twenty years of residence or marriage depending on your tie to Brunei, and it is granted at the authorities' discretion.

source.label: Immigration and National Registration Department of Brunei - permanent resident status via Entry Permit
source.authority: Immigration and National Registration Department, Ministry of Home Affairs (Brunei Darussalam)

routes.name: Dependent Pass (family of pass holders)
routes.summary: For you if your spouse or parent holds a Brunei work pass: the Dependent Pass lets close family live in Brunei for the validity of the main holder's pass - though it does not, by itself, let you work.
routes.duration: Tied to the validity of the main pass holder's pass and renewed alongside it; it is a stay route rather than a settlement route.

source.label: Immigration and National Registration Department of Brunei - dependent pass (Foreign Work Pass division)
source.authority: Immigration and National Registration Department, Ministry of Home Affairs (Brunei Darussalam)

routes.name: Student Pass (foreign students)
routes.summary: For you if you have a place to study in Brunei: the Student Pass lets you live in the country for the length of your course, linked to your enrolment at a recognised institution.
routes.duration: Linked to the length of your course and renewable while you remain enrolled; it is a study route rather than a settlement route.

source.label: Immigration and National Registration Department of Brunei - immigration services for foreigners
source.authority: Immigration and National Registration Department, Ministry of Home Affairs (Brunei Darussalam)

routes.name: Temporary Employment Permit (Work Permit)
routes.summary: For people moving to Belize for a job: this is the Temporary Employment Permit you apply for through the Labour Department to work lawfully for an employer in the country.
routes.duration: Commonly issued for one year and renewable while the employment continues; a permit alone does not lead to settlement. Confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: Temporary Employment Permit (Work Permit) - Immigration Belize
source.authority: Labour Department / Immigration and Nationality Department (Belize)

routes.name: Qualified Retirement Program (QRP)
routes.summary: For retirees aged 40 and over with steady foreign retirement income: the QRP, run by the Belize Tourism Board, gives you residency in Belize - but heads-up, it is residency, not citizenship, and it does not normally count toward permanent residence.
routes.duration: Grants a QRP resident card renewed annually for as long as you keep qualifying; it is residency, not citizenship, and generally does not count toward permanent residence. Confirm current conditions on the official page.

source.label: Retirement Program (QRP) - Belize Tourism Board

routes.name: Temporary Residence
routes.summary: For people building a life in Belize: temporary residence is the status you hold while you live in the country and work toward permanent residence through the Immigration and Nationality Department.
routes.duration: Held during your legal residence in Belize and renewed as required; it leads toward permanent residence once the qualifying period is completed. Confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: Residence - Immigration Belize

routes.name: Permanent Residence
routes.summary: For people settling in Belize: permanent residence can be reached after about a year of legal residence in the country - but only if you keep your absences within strict limits during that year.
routes.duration: Grants settled permanent residence; reachable after about a year of legal residence with strict absence limits. Confirm current validity and renewal on the official page.

source.label: Residence (Permanent Residence) - Immigration Belize

routes.name: Family Residence (Spouse and Dependants)
routes.summary: For spouses and dependants of someone settled in Belize: this family route lets you live in the country based on your relationship to a Belizean or a resident.
routes.duration: Grants residence based on the family relationship and can lead toward permanent residence; confirm current validity and renewal on the official page.

source.label: Residence (family) and Dependent Permit - Immigration Belize

routes.name: Student Permit
routes.summary: For international students: this is the permit you need to study in Belize, which you must obtain before your school year or semester begins.
routes.duration: Issued for a school year at primary and secondary level, or a semester at tertiary level, and renewed while you remain enrolled; it does not lead to settlement. Confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: Student Permit - Immigration Belize

routes.name: Tourist Visa
routes.summary: Bangladesh visitor route for tourism, casual visits, seminars, study tours and similar short non-work purposes.
routes.duration: A tourist visa may be issued for up to 3 months with single entry; extension up to 1 month can be sought from the Department of Immigration & Passports in Dhaka.

source.label: Tourist Visa - Bangladesh High Commission London

routes.name: Business Visa
routes.summary: Bangladesh route for businesspeople visiting for trade, commerce and investment-related business activity.
routes.duration: A business visa may be issued for up to 1 year with single, double or multiple entries; each visit should be no more than 60 days. Extension may be available from DIP up to 3 years, generally with up to 6 months stay per visit.

source.label: Business Visa - Bangladesh High Commission London

routes.name: Investor Visa
routes.summary: Bangladesh route for investors in existing, new, under-construction or upcoming private-sector industrial or commercial entities.
routes.duration: An investor visa may be issued for up to 1 year with single, double or multiple entries. Extension up to 5 years can be obtained from DIP in Bangladesh.

source.label: Investor Visa - Bangladesh High Commission London

routes.name: Work permit/Employment Visa
routes.summary: Bangladesh work route for appointed experts, advisers, employees, contractors and qualifying NGO honorary workers.
routes.duration: A work permit/employment visa may be issued for up to 3 months with single, double or multiple entries, with a maximum 90-day stay per visit. Extension up to 3 years can be obtained from DIP in Bangladesh.

source.label: Work permit/Employment Visa - Bangladesh High Commission London

routes.name: Student Visa
routes.summary: Bangladesh study route for regular students, admission seekers and researchers at government-approved educational institutions.
routes.duration: A student visa may be issued for up to 1 year with multiple entries. Extension up to the course tenure can be obtained from DIP in Bangladesh.

source.label: Student Visa - Bangladesh High Commission London

routes.name: Visa on Arrival
routes.summary: Bangladesh on-arrival route for eligible government, tourism, business, investment, Bangladesh-origin and official travellers.
routes.duration: Visa on arrival is for a maximum of 30 days.

source.label: Visa on Arrival and Transit Visa - Bangladesh High Commission London

routes.name: No Visa Required (NVR)
routes.summary: Bangladesh NVR endorsement for qualifying Bangladesh-origin foreign nationals and certain spouses or children.
routes.duration: NVR is an endorsement in the passport; its validity and entry effect follow the endorsement issued and the instructions of the responsible Bangladesh mission. Check the endorsement before travel.

routes.name: Permanent Residence (Residencia Permanente)

routes.name: Z Work Visa (with Foreigner Work Permit and Residence Permit)
routes.summary: For you if a Chinese employer has offered you a job: the Z visa is the standard route into paid work in mainland China, used together with a Foreigner Work Permit and, after arrival, a residence permit.
routes.duration: The Z visa itself is short-validity for entry; the work-type residence permit you obtain after arrival is typically issued for one year and renewable.

source.label: National Immigration Administration - services portal for foreigners

routes.name: K Visa (young science and technology talent)
routes.summary: For you if you are a young scientist, engineer or technologist: the K visa is a new route (effective 1 October 2025) that lets eligible STEM talent enter China without a domestic employer first inviting you - but read the honesty note below: its work-authorisation status is still being clarified.
routes.duration: Indicative only. The K visa is described as offering more flexibility on entries, validity and length of stay than the existing ordinary categories; confirm the current terms on the official page.

source.label: State Council of China - K visa for young science and technology talent
source.authority: State Council of the People's Republic of China

routes.name: R Talent Visa (high-level and urgently needed talent)
routes.summary: For you if you are a recognised high-level expert or have skills China urgently needs: the R visa is the talent route, normally used alongside a top-tier Foreigner Work Permit and, after arrival, a residence permit.
routes.duration: The R visa is for entry; the work-type residence permit obtained after arrival is typically issued for one or more years and is renewable.

source.label: National Immigration Administration - services portal for foreigners

routes.name: Foreign Permanent Resident ID Card (Five-Star Card)
routes.summary: For you if you want to settle in China long term: the Foreign Permanent Resident ID Card - nicknamed the Five-Star Card - is China's actual permanent residence document, issued by the National Immigration Administration once your permanent-residence application is approved.
routes.duration: Permanent residence status; the physical card is issued with a validity period and is renewed while you maintain eligibility.

source.label: National Immigration Administration — Permanent residence eligibility, procedure and fees

routes.name: Q Family Reunion Visa (Q1 and Q2)
routes.summary: For you if you are family of a Chinese citizen or a permanent resident of China: the Q visa is the family-reunion route, with a long-stay Q1 (leading to a residence permit) and a short-stay Q2 for visits.
routes.duration: Q1 is a long-stay route: after entry you obtain a family-type residence permit, often issued for up to several years and renewable. Q2 is for short visits only.

source.label: National Immigration Administration - services portal for foreigners

routes.name: X Student Visa (X1 and X2)
routes.summary: For you if you have been accepted to study in mainland China: the X visa is the student route, with X1 for longer courses (over six months, leading to a residence permit) and X2 for shorter study.
routes.duration: X1 covers long courses: after entry you obtain a study-type residence permit for the programme length, renewable while you study. X2 is for short study of up to six months.

source.label: National Immigration Administration - services portal for foreigners

routes.name: M Business Visa
routes.summary: For you if you are travelling to mainland China for commercial or trade activities: the M visa covers business trips such as meetings, negotiations and trade fairs - but it is not a work visa and does not let you take up employment.
routes.duration: Short stays per visit; the visa can be single, double or multiple entry depending on what is granted.

source.label: National Immigration Administration - services portal for foreigners

routes.name: Temporary Residence for Work (RT-3)

routes.duration: Generally granted for one year and renewable while the employment continues; tied to the work contract. Confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: Residencia Temporal Laboral (RT-3) - DGM

routes.name: Residence by Investment - Pensionado (Retiree)
routes.summary: If you receive a pension from abroad, the pensionado route gives you Dominican residence quickly - and it puts you on the fast track to permanent residence from your first card.
routes.duration: A fast-track residence route: pensioners are typically granted a permanent-residence card from the first card rather than a long temporary period. Confirm current terms on the official page.

source.label: Residencia por Inversion en calidad de Jubilado o Pensionado - DGM

routes.name: Residence by Investment - Rentista (Annuitant)
routes.summary: If you have steady income from abroad - including remote work - the rentista route is the Dominican Republic's practical home for you, and it leads quickly to permanent residence.
routes.duration: A fast-track residence route: rentistas are typically granted a permanent-residence card from the first card rather than a long temporary period. Confirm current terms on the official page.

source.label: Residencia por Inversion en calidad de Rentista - DGM

routes.name: Residence by Investment - Investor
routes.summary: If you make a qualifying investment in the Dominican Republic, the investor route gives you residence and, like the other investment classes, a fast track to permanent residence.
routes.duration: A fast-track residence route: investors are typically granted a permanent-residence card from the first card rather than a long temporary period. Confirm current terms on the official page.

source.label: Residencia en calidad de Inversionista - DGM

routes.name: Ordinary Temporary Residence (RT-9)
routes.summary: If your reason for living in the Dominican Republic does not fit a work or investment category, ordinary RT-9 temporary residence is the general route - renewed yearly on the way to permanent residence.
routes.duration: Generally granted for one year and renewed annually; the standard path is to renew RT-9 for the required period before changing to permanent residence. Confirm current terms on the official page.

source.label: Residencia Temporal (RT-9) - DGM

routes.name: Permanent Residence (RP-1)
routes.summary: Permanent residence (RP-1) is the Dominican Republic's settled-status card - reached fast through the investment classes, or after the required years of renewed temporary residence on the ordinary route.

source.label: Solicitud de Residencia Permanente (RP-1) - DGM

routes.summary: A renewable residence permit granted to foreigners who own qualifying property in Egypt, with the validity period scaling by the value of the property; renewable but never permanent.

source.label: Residence Permits - Ministry of Interior (Egypt)

routes.name: Residence Permit via Bank Deposit (Egypt)
routes.summary: A renewable residence permit for foreigners who place a qualifying deposit in an Egyptian state-owned bank, with the validity period scaling by the size of the deposit; renewable but never permanent.
routes.duration: Renewable validity that scales with the deposit size (commonly one or three years); never permanent.

source.label: Residence Permits - Ministry of Interior (Egypt)

routes.name: Student Residence Permit (Egypt)
routes.summary: A residence permit for foreign nationals enrolled at an Egyptian school, university or institute, valid for the study period and renewable, but never permanent.

source.label: Residence Permits - Ministry of Interior (Egypt)

routes.name: Family Residence Permit (Egypt)
routes.summary: A residence permit for the spouse and dependent children of an Egyptian national or a foreign resident, tied to the family relationship and renewable, but never permanent.

routes.name: Temporary Residence - Digital Nomad (Visa Nomada)

routes.name: India Student Visa
