routes.duration: Up to five years or the academic-course duration, whichever is shorter; generally up to four entries per academic year.

source.label: Ministry of Home Affairs - Details of visas granted by India

routes.name: Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) Card
routes.summary: Lifelong multiple-entry status for foreign nationals of Indian origin and their eligible relatives.
routes.duration: Lifelong, subject to re-issue conditions for cards issued before age 20 and after age 50.

source.label: Online OCI Services

routes.name: B/1 Expert Work Visa
routes.summary: Employer-sponsored work visa for foreign experts whose specialist skills are not readily available in the Israeli labour market. The Israeli employer must first obtain a permit from PIBA before the visa is issued.
routes.duration: Issued for fixed periods (commonly up to one year), renewable subject to PIBA approval; verify current durations on the official page.

source.label: Apply for a permit to employ an expert foreign worker - PIBA

routes.name: Aliyah - Immigration under the Law of Return
routes.summary: Immigration to Israel under the Law of Return, open to Jews, their children and grandchildren, and eligible spouses, leading to Israeli citizenship.
routes.duration: Leads to Israeli citizenship; an A/1 temporary residence visa for eligible persons is issued for a multi-year period as an alternative pathway. Verify on the official page.

source.label: Apply for a Temporary Residence Visa Type A/1 under the Right of Return - PIBA

routes.name: A/2 Student Visa
routes.summary: Temporary stay permit for students enrolled at Israeli schools, academic institutions, yeshivas or recognised youth institutions. Holders may not work in Israel.
routes.duration: Up to one year, renewable for the duration of the course of study; verify on the official page.

source.label: Apply for an entry visa for students or yeshiva pupils - PIBA

routes.name: Status through Marriage to an Israeli Citizen or Permanent Resident
routes.name_fa: اقامت همسر یا شریک زندگی؛ دائم
routes.summary: Graduated procedure through which the foreign spouse or partner of an Israeli citizen or permanent resident obtains legal status, progressing over several years toward permanent residence or citizenship.
routes.duration: A graduated, multi-year process leading over time toward permanent residence or citizenship; exact duration depends on circumstances. Verify on the official page.

source.label: Application for legal status by virtue of a marital relationship with an Israeli - PIBA

routes.name: Work KITAS (Limited Stay Permit)
routes.summary: Employer-sponsored limited stay permit (ITAS/KITAS) that lets a foreign professional live and work for a registered Indonesian company.
routes.duration: Commonly issued for periods of up to about two years, renewable while employment continues.

source.label: Stay permits (Izin Tinggal Keimigrasian) - Directorate General of Immigration

routes.name: Investor KITAS (Limited Stay Permit for Investors)
routes.summary: Limited stay permit for foreign shareholders or directors of a PT PMA (foreign-investment company) in Indonesia.
routes.duration: Commonly issued for periods of up to about two years, renewable while the qualifying investment and role continue.

source.label: Stay permits (Izin Tinggal Keimigrasian) - Directorate General of Immigration

routes.name: Golden Visa (5 and 10-year)
routes.summary: Long-stay investor and talent visa granting 5 or 10 years of residence to qualifying investors, corporate figures and selected individuals.
routes.duration: Granted for 5 or 10 years depending on the qualifying tier, renewable.

source.label: Golden Visa Indonesia - Directorate General of Immigration

routes.name: Second Home Visa
routes.summary: Long-stay visa for self-funded foreigners and retirees who can show substantial funds or qualifying property in Indonesia.
routes.duration: Issued for multi-year periods (commonly a 5 or 10-year track), renewable subject to conditions.

source.label: Second Home Visa - Official eVisa website for Indonesia

routes.name: Family / Spouse KITAS
routes.summary: Limited stay permit for the foreign spouse or dependent family of an Indonesian citizen or of a KITAS/KITAP holder.
routes.duration: Commonly issued for periods of up to about two years, renewable while the family relationship continues.

source.label: Stay permits (Izin Tinggal Keimigrasian) - Directorate General of Immigration

routes.name: Student KITAS (Limited Stay Permit for Study)
routes.summary: Limited stay permit for foreign students enrolled at an accredited Indonesian educational institution.
routes.duration: Aligned to the study programme, commonly up to about one or two years and renewable while enrolled.

source.label: Stay permits (Izin Tinggal Keimigrasian) - Directorate General of Immigration

routes.name: KITAP (Permanent Stay Permit)
routes.summary: Indonesia's permanent stay permit, available to long-term KITAS holders such as spouses of citizens, investors and retirees.
routes.duration: Issued for a multi-year period and renewable, with provisions for extended validity.

source.label: Stay permits (Izin Tinggal Keimigrasian) - Directorate General of Immigration

routes.name: Residence Permit for Qualified Professionals (Iceland)
routes.summary: If you are a qualified professional or expert with an Icelandic job offer, this is the main route - a two-step residence permit plus a linked work permit.
routes.duration: The expert-work residence permit may be granted for up to four years, but not beyond the validity of the work permit. Check the actual expiry dates of both permissions.

source.label: Island.is - Residence permit based on work

routes.name: Temporary Work Permit due to Labour Shortage (Iceland)
routes.summary: An employer-supported route for exceptional labour shortages. The work permit is temporary and employer-specific; the associated labour-shortage residence permission can qualify as a basis for permanent residence.
routes.duration: The first shortage work permit may last up to one year, or the shorter seasonal project period; renewals may be for up to two years. Check the separate residence-permit expiry and continuing conditions.

source.label: Island.is - Work permit due to shortage of employees

routes.name: Self-employment in Iceland: residence and work rights
routes.summary: Self-employment rights in Iceland depend on nationality and existing immigration status. Company ownership alone does not establish a residence route: distinguish EEA/EFTA registration, employer-linked permission and permanent-resident work rights.
routes.duration: Depends on the actual residence or registration basis; no separate general entrepreneur-permit term is established here.

source.label: Island.is - Work permits and exemptions

routes.name: Residence Permit for Family Reunification (Iceland)
routes.summary: Join an eligible family member in Iceland. Your relationship and the sponsor's exact status determine eligibility, work rights and whether your residence can count toward permanent residence.
routes.duration: Generally aligned to the sponsor's status and renewable - confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: Island.is - Spouse requirements; other family categories differ

routes.name: Residence Permit for Students (Iceland)
routes.summary: If you have been admitted to an Icelandic university or college, this residence permit lets you live in Iceland while you study.
routes.duration: Granted for up to one year at a time and renewable while you stay enrolled - confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: Island.is - Residence permit for students

routes.name: Long-Term Visa for Remote Work (Iceland)
routes.summary: If you work remotely for a foreign employer, this short long-term visa lets you stay in Iceland for a few months - but it is a visa, not a residence permit.
routes.duration: A single stay of 90 to 180 days, generally not repeatable within twelve months - confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: Work in Iceland - remote-work long-term visa (Directorate of Immigration)

routes.name: Permanent Residence Permit (Iceland)
routes.summary: Permanent residence normally follows four continuous qualifying years in Iceland, but family, study and other exceptions can change the route. Approval brings permanent stay and broad work rights, not automatic citizenship.
routes.duration: Permanent stay subject to residence conditions; the residence card is valid for five years and must be replaced when it expires.

source.label: Island.is - Permanent residence permit (requirements)

routes.name: Tourist eVisa
routes.summary: Online Iraq tourist eVisa route through the Ministry of Interior eVisa portal, currently presented as a tourism-only electronic application flow.
routes.duration: The eVisa portal describes the eVisa as valid for 30 days; applicants should confirm whether their approval is single-entry or multiple-entry in the issued document.

source.label: Iraq eVisa portal - about eVisa
source.authority: Republic of Iraq, Ministry of Interior eVisa Portal

routes.name: Visit or Tourism Consular Visa
routes.summary: Consular visit and tourism visa framework for Iraq, including tourism, religious visits and authorised business or investor visits.
routes.duration: MOFA describes tourist visa entry once during three months from grant with a one-month stay; visit visa wording also describes one-month entry and one-month residence for religious or holy-site visits.

source.label: Iraq Ministry of Foreign Affairs - Visa
source.authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Republic of Iraq

routes.name: Normal Visa
routes.summary: MOFA normal visa category allowing one entry within three months and residence in Iraq for up to three months, with arrival reporting to the Directorate of Residence.
routes.duration: One entry during three months from grant, with residence in Iraq not exceeding three months, according to the MOFA page.

source.label: Iraq Ministry of Foreign Affairs - Visa
source.authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Republic of Iraq

routes.name: Transit and Non-Stop Transit Visa
routes.summary: Iraq transit framework for short stopovers and supervised non-stop transit through Iraqi territory.
routes.duration: Transit visa: one entry within three months from grant and stay up to seven days. Non-stop transit: one supervised transit within three months without stopping.

source.label: Iraq Ministry of Foreign Affairs - Visa
source.authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Republic of Iraq

routes.name: Multi-Entry Visa
routes.summary: Iraq multi-entry visa category for repeated travel, granted for three months, six months or one year after legal conditions are met.
routes.duration: MOFA says multi-entry visas may be granted for three months, six months or one year after the legal conditions are met.

source.label: Iraq Ministry of Foreign Affairs - Visa
source.authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Republic of Iraq

routes.name: Work-Permit-Linked Visa or Residence Permit
routes.summary: Cautious employer-linked route note for foreign workers, because MOFA says worker visas and residence permits generally require a Ministry of Labor and Social Affairs work permit first.
routes.duration: The reviewed MOFA page does not publish a standard work-linked visa or residence-permit grant period; timing depends on the work permit, visa and residence channel used.

source.label: Iraq Ministry of Foreign Affairs - Visa
source.authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Republic of Iraq

routes.name: Visa-Waiver Tourism Entry
routes.summary: Visa-free tourism entry note for nationalities covered by Iran MFA waiver arrangements, including the listed 15-day ordinary-passport tourism waiver.
routes.duration: Up to 15 days for the MFA-listed ordinary-passport tourism waiver; other bilateral waivers depend on the nationality-specific rule.

source.label: Iran MFA eVisa portal - home
source.authority: Evisa Department, Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Iran

routes.name: Tourist Visa
routes.summary: Iran MFA tourist visa category for foreign citizens travelling to Iran for tourism, including ordinary eVisa and place-of-issue workflows shown by the portal.
routes.duration: Validity and permitted stay are shown on the issued visa; confirm the grant terms before travel.

source.label: Iran MFA eVisa - visa types
source.authority: Evisa Department, Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Iran

routes.name: Entry Visa
routes.summary: Iran MFA Entry Visa (A) for invited visits such as business negotiations, academic contacts, sport, official meetings and family visits by relatives of foreign residents.
routes.duration: Validity and permitted stay are shown on the issued visa or mission instruction.

source.label: Iran MFA eVisa - visa types
source.authority: Evisa Department, Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Iran

routes.name: Pilgrimage Visa
routes.summary: Iran MFA Pilgrimage Visa (C) for foreign Muslim pilgrims travelling to holy places in Iran.
routes.duration: Validity and stay length are shown on the issued pilgrimage visa.

source.label: Iran MFA eVisa - visa types
source.authority: Evisa Department, Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Iran

routes.name: Education Visa
routes.summary: Iran MFA Education Visa (E) for foreign students, religious scholars and researchers with eligibility certification from an Iranian authority or accredited institution.
routes.duration: Validity and stay conditions are set by the issued visa and the Iranian academic or ministry approval.

source.label: Iran MFA eVisa - visa types
source.authority: Evisa Department, Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Iran

routes.name: Temporary Work Visa
routes.summary: Iran MFA Temporary Work Visa (F) for skilled workers, specialists in fields such as medical and industrial work, and engineers with a sponsor employer and approved labour certificate.
routes.duration: Validity and work conditions are set by the issued visa and the approved labour certificate.

source.label: Iran MFA eVisa - visa types
source.authority: Evisa Department, Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Iran

routes.name: Transit Visa
routes.summary: Iran MFA Transit Visa (G) for foreign citizens passing through Iran with no purpose of stay.
routes.duration: Transit-only permission; validity and transit stay are shown on the issued visa.

source.label: Iran MFA eVisa - visa types
source.authority: Evisa Department, Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Iran

routes.name: Media Visa
routes.summary: Iran MFA Media Visa (H), labelled “Press” in the public application selector, for foreign media professionals with a Media and Public Diplomacy Center permit.
routes.duration: Validity and conditions are shown on the issued media visa and permit.

source.label: Iran MFA eVisa - visa types
source.authority: Evisa Department, Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Iran

routes.name: Investment Visa
routes.summary: Iran MFA Investment Visa (I) for foreign investors with an approval letter from the Organization for Investment Economic and Technical Assistance of Iran.
routes.duration: Validity and conditions are shown on the issued visa and investment approval.

source.label: Iran MFA eVisa - visa types
source.authority: Evisa Department, Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Iran

routes.name: Marital Visa
routes.summary: Iran MFA Marital Visa (M) for foreign men married to Iranian women and their offspring, with family permission evidence where required.
routes.duration: Validity and stay conditions are shown on the issued marital visa.

source.label: Iran MFA eVisa - visa types
source.authority: Evisa Department, Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Iran

routes.name: Medical Visa
routes.summary: Iran MFA Medical Visa (T) for foreign citizens travelling for treatment with approval from an authorised Iranian medical centre.
routes.duration: Validity and stay conditions are shown on the issued medical visa and treatment approval.

source.label: Iran MFA eVisa - visa types
source.authority: Evisa Department, Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Iran

routes.name: Immigration Permission and Visa Check
routes.summary: Isle of Man immigration check route for visitors, workers, students, families and business travellers using official Isle of Man Government guidance.
routes.duration: As granted for the relevant Isle of Man visit, work, study, family, settlement or business purpose.

source.label: Isle of Man Government - Immigration
source.authority: Immigration Service, Isle of Man Government

routes.name: Work Permit
routes.summary: Isle of Man work-permit authority route for employers and workers checking local permission before employment starts.
routes.duration: Permit duration and conditions depend on the official Isle of Man work-permit route and the permission granted.

source.label: Isle of Man Government - Work permits
source.authority: Work Permits, Isle of Man Government

routes.name: Immigration Rules and Associated Policy
routes.summary: Isle of Man rules-and-policy check for applicants who need the legal basis behind visit, work, settlement, study, business or family permission.
routes.duration: Depends on the immigration route and the permission granted under current Isle of Man rules or policy.

source.label: Isle of Man Government - Immigration
source.authority: Immigration Service, Isle of Man Government

routes.name: Study, Business or Settle Authority Check
routes.summary: Isle of Man authority-check route for study, business and settlement cases where the applicant needs current official direction before filing.
routes.duration: Purpose and permission dependent; check the current Isle of Man Government route for the exact grant and conditions.

source.label: Isle of Man Government - Immigration
source.authority: Immigration Service, Isle of Man Government

routes.name: Highly Skilled Professional (HSP) Visa
routes.summary: Points-based visa for highly skilled foreign professionals — the fastest route to Japanese permanent residence (1–3 years).
routes.duration: 5 years; with fast-track PR after 1–3 years.

source.label: ISA — Points-based system for Highly Skilled Foreign Professionals

routes.name: Engineer / Specialist in Humanities / International Services
routes.summary: Japan's most common work visa for knowledge workers — engineers, IT professionals, translators, designers, and business staff.
routes.duration: 1 or 3 years (5 years for renewals); renewable.

source.label: ISA — Engineer/Specialist in Humanities/Int'l Services

routes.name: Specified Skilled Worker Type 1 (SSW-1 / 特定技能1号)
routes.summary: Work visa for skilled workers in designated industries — requires passing a skills test and Japanese language test (JLPT N4+).
routes.duration: Up to 5 years total (not renewable beyond 5 years — must transition to SSW-2 or another status).

source.label: ISA — Specified Skilled Worker support site

routes.name: Business Manager Visa (経営・管理)
routes.summary: Visa for foreign nationals starting or managing a business in Japan — now requires a physical office, at least ¥30 million in capital or business funds, and at least one qualifying full-time employee.
routes.duration: 1 year initially; renewable for 1, 3, or 5 years.

source.label: ISA — Business Manager

routes.name: Student Visa (留学)
routes.summary: Visa for international students at Japanese universities, language schools, and vocational institutions — includes part-time work rights.
routes.duration: Individual period of stay set by the Minister of Justice, not exceeding 4 years 3 months; renew/change status as circumstances require.

source.label: ISA — Student

routes.name: Work Permit (Ministry of Labour)
routes.summary: For people moving to Jamaica with a job: this is the Ministry of Labour work permit your employer (or, for investors, JAMPRO) applies for so you can work legally.
routes.duration: Granted for a designated period set in the permit letter and renewable while the employment continues. Confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: Work Permit - Ministry of Labour and Social Security
source.authority: Ministry of Labour and Social Security (Jamaica)

routes.name: Permanent Residence via Employment
routes.summary: For people who have worked in Jamaica for several years: this PICA route lets long-term workers settle permanently rather than keep renewing temporary status.
routes.duration: Settled residence status once granted; applications are commonly described as taking around three to six months to process. Confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: Permanent Residence - Passport, Immigration and Citizenship Agency

routes.name: Permanent Residence for Retirees
routes.summary: For retirees settling in Jamaica: this PICA route lets retired foreign nationals live in Jamaica permanently on pension or other independent income.
routes.duration: Settled residence status once granted; applications are commonly described as taking around three to six months to process. Confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: Permanent Residence - Passport, Immigration and Citizenship Agency

routes.name: Unconditional Landing
routes.summary: For people with a Jamaican connection: this PICA stamp lets you live, work and study in Jamaica without a work permit or student visa - by descent, naturalisation or as a CARICOM skilled national.
routes.duration: The stamp lasts until the foreign passport expires, subject to PICA's current requirements; the application page asks for a passport with at least six months remaining. Transfer the stamp when the passport is renewed and confirm the current procedure with PICA.

source.label: Unconditional Landing - Passport, Immigration and Citizenship Agency

routes.name: Remote Work Stay (oriented to US passport holders)
routes.summary: For remote workers - mainly US passport holders - who want to live in Jamaica while working for an overseas employer or clients, registered through PICA rather than on a universal digital-nomad visa.
routes.duration: Arranged through PICA extension of stay; commonly described as an initial period that can be extended. Confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: Extension of Stays - Passport, Immigration and Citizenship Agency

routes.name: Marriage Exemption Certificate (spouse of a Jamaican)
routes.summary: For people married to a Jamaican: a Marriage Exemption Certificate lets you work in Jamaica without a work permit, with your stay endorsed by PICA.
routes.duration: Held while the certificate is valid; PICA endorses the matching stay in your passport. Confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: Extension of Stays (Marriage Exemption Certificate endorsement) - Passport, Immigration and Citizenship Agency

routes.name: Student Stay (Extension of Stay for Students)
routes.summary: For international students in Jamaica: PICA endorses your stay for the length of your course at an accredited institution, so you can study without a work permit.
routes.duration: Granted to cover the duration of your programme of study, or up to your passport's expiry. Confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: Extension of Stays (students) - Passport, Immigration and Citizenship Agency

routes.name: Work Residency (Employer-Sponsored)
routes.summary: For people moving to Jordan with a job: this is the employer-sponsored residence permit you hold alongside a Ministry of Labour work permit so you can live and work in Jordan.
routes.duration: Generally valid for one year and renewed annually while the employment and work permit continue. Confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: Residence Permits E-Applications (Work Residency) - Ministry of Interior

routes.name: Annual Residence for Five Years (Renewable)
routes.summary: For long-settled foreigners and property owners: this renewable five-year residence permit gives a longer, more stable stay than the annual permit - but it is renewable, not a permanent-residence card.
routes.duration: Granted as a renewable five-year residence permit; it is not permanent residence. Confirm current validity and renewal conditions on the official page.

source.label: Granting a Five-Year Residence Permit - Ministry of Interior (Jordan e-Government)

routes.name: Investor Residency (Qualifying Real-Estate Purchase)
routes.summary: For people buying qualifying property in Jordan: this residency lets a real-estate investor and their family live in Jordan based on a property purchase that meets the threshold.
routes.duration: A renewable residence permit tied to continued ownership of the qualifying property; it is a residence route, not citizenship. Confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: Residence Permits E-Applications (Investor / property residence) - Ministry of Interior

routes.name: Self-Funded ("Workless") Residency with Bank Deposit
routes.summary: For people who can support themselves in Jordan without working: this residency is based on your own funds (a bank deposit), with the deposit rules recently eased for long-term property owners.
routes.duration: A renewable residence permit while the deposit (or property) condition is maintained. Confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: Residence Permits E-Applications (Workless Residency with Bank Deposit) - Ministry of Interior

routes.name: Family / Follower Residency
routes.summary: For families joining a resident in Jordan: this "follower" residency lets a spouse and children reside with a primary residence-permit holder or a Jordanian family member.
routes.duration: Generally valid for one year and renewed annually, tied to the primary resident's status. Confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: Residence Permits E-Applications (Family / Follower Residency) - Ministry of Interior

routes.name: Study Residency
routes.summary: For international students in Jordan: this residence permit lets you live in Jordan while you study at a recognised institution, renewed as your studies continue.
routes.duration: Generally valid for one year and renewed annually as your studies continue. Confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: Residence Permits E-Applications (Study Residency) - Ministry of Interior

routes.name: Immigration Permission and Visa
routes.summary: Jersey immigration-permission route for travellers checking whether they need a visa or permission to visit, work, study or live in Jersey.
routes.duration: As granted for the visit, study, work or residence purpose.

source.label: Government of Jersey - Moving to Jersey: apply for a visa
source.authority: Jersey Customs and Immigration Service, Government of Jersey

routes.name: Work Permit
routes.summary: Employer-led Jersey work-permit route for people who are not British or Irish and need immigration permission to work in Jersey.
routes.duration: Temporary route may be 9 or 12 months in relevant sectors; long-term route can be up to 3 years initially, with some medical doctor permits up to 5 years.

source.label: Government of Jersey - Work permit policy
source.authority: Jersey Customs and Immigration Service, Government of Jersey

routes.name: Register as a Jersey Resident
routes.summary: Register online after moving to Jersey, or use the existing-card service if you already have a Social Security number. Check the age and status conditions before paying.
routes.duration: Arrival registration and ongoing card updates, not a grant of immigration leave.

source.label: Government of Jersey — resident registration

routes.name: Residential and Employment Status
routes.summary: Jersey status framework determining where a person can live and work through Entitled, Licensed, Entitled for Work and Registered categories.
routes.duration: Status depends on residence history, employment permission, relationship basis or business permission; some Entitled status can become permanent after qualifying residence.

source.label: Government of Jersey - Residential and employment statuses

routes.name: Customs and Immigration Arrival
routes.summary: Jersey arrival compliance route for people moving with belongings, vehicles, pets or work plans.
routes.duration: Arrival and import compliance applies at or before the move to Jersey.

source.label: Government of Jersey - Customs and immigration
source.authority: Jersey Customs and Immigration Service, Government of Jersey

routes.name: E-7 Designated Activities Visa
routes.summary: Work visa for foreign professionals in specialised occupations — Korea's primary employer-sponsored route for skilled workers.
routes.duration: 1–3 years; renewable.

source.label: Hi Korea — E-7 visa information

routes.name: F-2-7 Points-Based Long-Term Residence
routes.summary: Points-based long-term residence for skilled professionals scoring 80+ points — the bridge between work visas and permanent residence in Korea.
routes.duration: 3 years; renewable.

source.label: Hi Korea — F-2-7 points-based residence

routes.name: D-8 Corporate Investment Visa
routes.summary: Visa for foreign nationals investing in or managing a Korean corporation — requires minimum investment and creates a pathway to long-term residence.
routes.duration: 1–2 years; renewable as long as the business operates.

source.label: Invest Korea — Foreign investment

routes.name: Student Visa (D-2)
routes.summary: Visa for international students at Korean universities — includes part-time work rights and a post-graduation job-seeking extension.
routes.duration: Duration of programme; renewed annually.

source.label: Study in Korea — Information portal

routes.name: F-1 Family Visitation / F-3 Dependent Family
routes.summary: Residence permits for family members of work-visa and student-visa holders in Korea — F-3 for dependents of E-series workers, F-1 for extended family visits.
routes.duration: Tied to the sponsoring family member's visa status.

source.label: Hi Korea — Family visas

routes.name: Class D Work Permit (Employment)
routes.summary: Employer-sponsored work permit for a foreign national offered specific employment by a specific Kenyan employer, where the skills are not available locally.
routes.duration: Issued and renewable in line with the employment; counts toward the residence record for permanent residence.

source.label: Class D (Employment) - Directorate of Immigration Services

routes.name: Class G Work Permit (Trade, Business or Consultancy)
routes.summary: Work permit for a foreign national investing in and running a specific trade, business, consultancy or profession in Kenya.
routes.duration: Issued and renewable in line with the business; counts toward the residence record for permanent residence.

source.label: Class G (Specific trade, business or consultancy) - Directorate of Immigration Services

routes.name: Class K Permit (Ordinary Residents)
routes.summary: Residence permit for a foreign national aged 35 or over with an assured income from sources outside Kenya, who undertakes not to take up employment.
routes.duration: Issued and renewable subject to continued assured income; counts toward the residence record for permanent residence.

source.label: Class K (Ordinary residents) - Directorate of Immigration Services

routes.name: Class A Work Permit (Prospecting and Mining)
routes.summary: Work permit for a foreign national engaging, alone or in partnership, in prospecting for minerals or mining in Kenya.
routes.duration: Issued and renewable in line with the licensed activity; counts toward the residence record for permanent residence.

source.label: Application for Permit Class A (Prospecting and Mining) - eFNS

routes.name: Special Pass
routes.summary: Short-term pass allowing a foreign national to conduct business, trade or a profession in Kenya temporarily, for up to six months.
routes.duration: Up to 6 months maximum; not a settlement route.

source.label: Special Pass - Directorate of Immigration Services

routes.name: Dependant's Pass
routes.summary: Pass for a dependant of a Kenyan citizen, a work-permit holder, a permanent resident or an exempted person.
routes.duration: Aligned to the sponsor status; renewable while the relationship and sponsor status continue.

source.label: Dependant's Pass - Directorate of Immigration Services

routes.name: Student's Pass
routes.summary: Pass for a foreign national admitted to an academic or training institution in Kenya.
routes.duration: Aligned to the course of study; renewable while enrolled.

source.label: Student's Pass - Directorate of Immigration Services

routes.name: Permanent Residence
routes.summary: Permanent residence in Kenya under the Kenya Citizenship and Immigration Act, including a route after long lawful residence on work permits.
routes.duration: Permanent on grant, subject to the conditions of the Act.

source.label: Permanent Residence - Directorate of Immigration Services

routes.name: Cayman Islands Work Permit (WORC)
routes.summary: If a Cayman Islands employer wants to hire you, this is the permit that lets you work for them. The employer applies through WORC, normally after advertising the role locally.
routes.duration: Granted for a defined term tied to a specific employer and post, and renewable subject to term limits; confirm current bands on the official page.

source.label: Work Permit and Permanent Residency FAQ - WORC

routes.name: Residency Certificate for Persons of Independent Means
routes.summary: If you have substantial means and want to live in the Cayman Islands without working, this long-validity certificate lets you reside there - but it does not give you permanent residence.
routes.duration: Issued for a long term (commonly 25 years) and renewable, but it does NOT confer permanent residence; it carries no right to work. Confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: Residency Certificate for Persons of Independent Means - WORC

routes.name: Certificate of Permanent Residence for Persons of Independent Means
routes.summary: If you make a very large real-estate investment in the Cayman Islands, this is the one independent-means route that actually grants permanent residence - but it is rare, expensive and quota-limited.
routes.duration: Permanent residence (settled status) once granted, subject to maintaining the qualifying investment; allocations are subject to an annual quota. Confirm current conditions on the official page.

source.label: Certificate of Permanent Residence for Persons of Independent Means - WORC

routes.name: Global Citizen Concierge Programme (GCCP)
routes.summary: If you work remotely for an employer abroad, the Global Citizen Concierge certificate was the Cayman route to live there while doing so - but its status is currently unclear, so check whether it is open before relying on it.
routes.duration: When open, granted for up to a defined period (reported as up to two years); it is a temporary remote-work certificate and does not lead to permanent residence. Verify the live status before relying on it.

source.label: Work Permit and Permanent Residency FAQ - WORC

routes.name: St Kitts and Nevis CBI - Sustainable Island State Contribution
routes.summary: For people who want to become a citizen of St Kitts and Nevis by making a one-time, non-refundable contribution to the government, rather than buying property. This is the country's main donation route.
routes.duration: Full citizenship, granted for life and transmissible to future generations, once the contribution is made and the application is approved.

source.label: Economic Citizenship - Government of St Kitts and Nevis
source.authority: Government of St Kitts and Nevis

routes.name: St Kitts and Nevis CBI - Approved Real Estate
routes.summary: For people who would rather own an asset than make a donation: you buy into a government-approved property development in St Kitts and Nevis and, in return, you and your family can apply for citizenship.
routes.duration: Full citizenship for life; the qualifying property must be held for a minimum period (historically several years) before it can be resold under the programme.

source.label: Economic Citizenship - Government of St Kitts and Nevis
source.authority: Government of St Kitts and Nevis

routes.name: St Kitts and Nevis CBI - Public Benefit Option
routes.summary: For people who want citizenship of St Kitts and Nevis by backing an approved national project - such as infrastructure or development works - through a unit in a public-benefit scheme.
routes.duration: Full citizenship, granted for life and transmissible to future generations, once the qualifying investment is made and the application is approved.

source.label: Economic Citizenship - Government of St Kitts and Nevis
source.authority: Government of St Kitts and Nevis

routes.name: St Kitts and Nevis Work Permit
routes.summary: For people who have a job offer from an employer in St Kitts and Nevis. Your employer applies on your behalf to the Department of Labour, usually after advertising the role locally first.
routes.duration: A temporary, employer-tied permit, typically issued for a defined period and renewable; it does not by itself lead to settlement.

source.label: Work Visa Procurement - Government of St Kitts and Nevis
source.authority: Government of St Kitts and Nevis

routes.name: St Kitts and Nevis Permanent Residence
routes.summary: For people who want to settle long-term in St Kitts and Nevis through the ordinary residence rules - for example after a qualifying period of living there, or through marriage to a citizen - rather than through investment.
routes.duration: Indefinite right to reside once granted; a separate work permit may still be needed to work.

source.label: Government of St Kitts and Nevis - official portal
source.authority: Government of St Kitts and Nevis

routes.name: Work Permit and Residence (employer-sponsored)
routes.summary: For you if a Kazakhstani employer has offered you a job: this is the standard route into paid work in Kazakhstan, where your employer secures a work permit for you and you then hold a temporary residence permit to live there.
routes.duration: Work permits are tied to your employment and renewed while you keep the job; the residence permit is issued for a defined period and renewed alongside it.

source.label: eGov.kz - Services for foreigners in Kazakhstan
source.authority: Electronic Government of the Republic of Kazakhstan

routes.name: Neo Nomad Visa (B12-1)
routes.summary: For you if you work remotely for clients or an employer outside Kazakhstan: the Neo Nomad Visa (category B12-1) lets you live in Kazakhstan while keeping your foreign income - but please read the honesty note, because this one does not lead to permanent residence.
routes.duration: Issued for up to around a year with the possibility of in-country extension; it is a stay route, not a settlement route.

source.label: eGov.kz - Visa classification to stay in the Republic of Kazakhstan
source.authority: Electronic Government of the Republic of Kazakhstan

routes.name: Digital Nomad Residency (IT specialists, via Astana Hub)
routes.summary: For you if you are a foreign IT specialist: the Digital Nomad Residency is a route, run through Astana Hub, that can lead to a permanent residence permit in Kazakhstan - and that is the key difference from the Neo Nomad Visa.
routes.duration: Designed as a long-horizon route for IT talent that can lead to a permanent residence permit; confirm the current validity terms on the official page.

source.label: eGov.kz - Permit for foreign IT specialists for permanent residence
source.authority: Electronic Government of the Republic of Kazakhstan

routes.name: Temporary Residence Permit
routes.summary: For you if you are staying in Kazakhstan for more than the short visa-free window: the temporary residence permit is the document that lets you live there for a defined purpose such as work, study, family or business.
routes.duration: Issued for a defined period linked to your purpose of stay and renewable while that purpose continues.

source.label: eGov.kz - Temporary residence permit for foreigners in the Republic of Kazakhstan
source.authority: Electronic Government of the Republic of Kazakhstan

routes.name: Permanent Residence Permit
routes.summary: For you if you want to settle in Kazakhstan long term: the permanent residence permit confirms your right to live there indefinitely, and a central requirement is showing that you can financially support yourself.
routes.duration: Confirms permanent residence; the physical permit is issued with a validity period and renewed while you keep your status.

source.label: eGov.kz - How to get residence permit in KZ
source.authority: Electronic Government of the Republic of Kazakhstan

routes.name: Study Residence (foreign students)
routes.summary: For you if you have a place to study in Kazakhstan: this is the route that lets you live there for the length of your course, normally on a temporary residence permit linked to your enrolment.
routes.duration: Linked to the length of your course and renewable while you remain enrolled.

source.label: eGov.kz - For foreigners: entrance to the Republic of Kazakhstan and citizenship
source.authority: Electronic Government of the Republic of Kazakhstan

routes.name: Family Residence (reunification)
routes.summary: For you if a close family member lives in Kazakhstan: this route lets you join them and live there, normally on a temporary residence permit based on your family relationship.
routes.duration: Issued for a defined period and renewable while the family relationship and basis continue; can lead towards permanent residence over time.

source.label: eGov.kz - For foreigners: entrance to the Republic of Kazakhstan and citizenship
source.authority: Electronic Government of the Republic of Kazakhstan

routes.name: EB Business Visa (E-class ordinary visa, business/employment)
routes.summary: For you if you are coming to Cambodia to work or do business: the EB is the most common long-stay visa, an extension of the E-class ordinary visa - but please read the honesty note, because working also needs a separate Work Permit.
routes.duration: Extensions are typically issued for 1, 3, 6 or 12 months and can be renewed indefinitely; there is no permanent-residence status to graduate into.

source.label: General Department of Immigration - public services
source.authority: General Department of Immigration, Ministry of Interior (Cambodia)

routes.name: EP Employment Visa (E-class qualified-worker sub-class)
routes.summary: For you if you are taking up employment in Cambodia: the EP is an E-class extension oriented towards qualified workers and employees - and, like the EB, it still needs a separate Work Permit before you can legally work.
routes.duration: Extensions are typically issued in periods such as 1, 3, 6 or 12 months and are renewable; there is no settled status to progress to.

source.label: General Department of Immigration - public services
source.authority: General Department of Immigration, Ministry of Interior (Cambodia)

routes.name: ER Retirement Visa (E-class retirement sub-class)
routes.summary: For you if you are retired and aged 55 or over: the ER is the E-class retirement sub-class that lets you live in Cambodia long term by renewing the visa - though it does not lead to permanent residence.
routes.duration: Extensions are typically issued in periods such as 6 or 12 months and renewed to stay long term; there is no permanent-residence status to reach.

source.label: General Department of Immigration - public services
source.authority: General Department of Immigration, Ministry of Interior (Cambodia)

routes.name: EG Job-Seeking Visa (E-class job-seeking sub-class)
routes.summary: For you if you are coming to Cambodia to look for work or get set up before a job starts: the EG is the E-class general sub-class often used while you are job-seeking - and it does not, on its own, let you work.
routes.duration: Extensions are typically issued in shorter periods such as 1, 3 or 6 months while you are getting established; renewable, with no settled status to reach.

source.label: General Department of Immigration - public services
source.authority: General Department of Immigration, Ministry of Interior (Cambodia)

routes.name: ES Student Visa (E-class student sub-class)
routes.summary: For you if you are studying in Cambodia: the ES is the E-class student sub-class, letting you stay for your studies by renewing the visa with a letter from a registered school.
routes.duration: Renewable for the length of your studies as long as you stay enrolled at a registered school; no permanent-residence status to reach.

source.label: General Department of Immigration - public services
source.authority: General Department of Immigration, Ministry of Interior (Cambodia)

routes.name: Article 18 Work Residency (private-sector Iqama)
routes.summary: For people taking a private-sector job in Kuwait. Your Kuwaiti employer sponsors you and the residency (the Iqama) is tied to that job. Note up front: Kuwait has no permanent residence for expatriates, and every residency here is fixed-term and sponsor-tied.
routes.duration: Fixed-term and renewed by your employer while the job continues; general residency permits run for limited terms (the 2025 reform sets general residency at up to five years). Confirm the current term on the official Ministry of Interior page.

source.label: General Directorate of Residency - e-services
source.authority: Ministry of Interior - General Directorate of Residency Affairs (Kuwait)

routes.name: Article 17 Government Work Residency
routes.summary: Government-sponsored residence for expatriate employees of a Kuwaiti government entity. Government-work entry, Article 17 residence and Civil ID registration are separate stages; this is not private-sector employment or an automatic permanent-residence route.
routes.duration: Ordinary residence may be granted for up to five years, subject to the actual government-supported grant and health-insurance coverage; renewal is not automatic.

source.label: Government residence: first issue, renewal and transfers
source.authority: Kuwait Government Online / Ministry of Interior

routes.name: Article 22 Family / Dependent Residency
routes.summary: For the spouse and children of someone already resident in Kuwait. The resident family member sponsors you, and the residency is tied to their status - like all Kuwaiti residency it is fixed-term, with no permanent residence for expatriates.
routes.duration: Fixed-term and linked to the sponsor's residency; renewed alongside it. Confirm the current term on the official Ministry of Interior page.

source.label: Family Residence Visa - Kuwait Government Online
source.authority: Kuwait Government Online / Ministry of Interior

routes.name: Investor Residency (long-term, up to ~15 years)
routes.summary: For foreign investors licensed under Kuwait's foreign-investment law, who can be granted a long-term residency of up to around 15 years. Important: even this long tier is renewable fixed-term residence, not permanent residence - Kuwait grants none to expatriates.
routes.duration: Long-term renewable residency of up to around 15 years for qualifying licensed investors; still fixed-term, not permanent. Confirm the current term on the official Ministry of Interior page.

source.label: General Directorate of Residency - e-services
source.authority: Ministry of Interior - General Directorate of Residency Affairs (Kuwait)

routes.name: Property-Owner Residency (long-term, up to ~10 years)
routes.summary: For foreign nationals who own qualifying real estate in Kuwait, who can be granted residency of up to around 10 years. As with every Kuwaiti residency, this is renewable fixed-term residence, not permanent residence.
routes.duration: Long-term renewable residency of up to around 10 years for qualifying property owners; still fixed-term, not permanent. Confirm the current term on the official Ministry of Interior page.

source.label: General Directorate of Residency - e-services
source.authority: Ministry of Interior - General Directorate of Residency Affairs (Kuwait)

routes.name: Student Residency
routes.summary: For foreign students enrolled at a recognised educational institution in Kuwait. The residency is study-linked and fixed-term, and as with all Kuwaiti residency there is no permanent residence for expatriates.
routes.duration: Fixed-term and renewed for the duration of your course of study. Confirm the current term on the official Ministry of Interior page.

source.label: General Directorate of Residency - e-services
source.authority: Ministry of Interior - General Directorate of Residency Affairs (Kuwait)

routes.name: Tourist eVisa
routes.summary: Official Kyrgyz Republic electronic visa route for eligible tourist travellers.
routes.duration: As issued in the eVisa approval; confirm the validity, stay length and entries in the portal before travel.

source.authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Kyrgyz Republic

routes.name: Speed Up eVisa Application Review

source.label: Kyrgyz Republic eVisa application review service
source.authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Kyrgyz Republic

routes.name: Airport Private, Tourism or Research Visa
routes.summary: Comoros short-stay airport visa route for private visits, tourism and research, based on the official embassy visa page.
routes.duration: The embassy source describes a short-stay visa that cannot exceed one month; confirm current validity and entry conditions before travel.

source.authority: Embassy of the Union of the Comoros in Belgium

routes.name: Business Visa
routes.summary: Comoros business visa route for investment-project and business visitors using the official embassy checklist.
routes.duration: Confirm validity and stay length with the embassy before filing or travelling.

source.label: Comoros embassy - business visa
source.authority: Embassy of the Union of the Comoros in Belgium

routes.name: Courtesy Visa
routes.summary: Comoros courtesy visa route for diplomatic or service passport holders using the official embassy requirements.
routes.duration: Confirm validity, passport-validity rules and mission dates with the embassy or sponsoring institution before travel.

source.label: Comoros embassy - courtesy visa
source.authority: Embassy of the Union of the Comoros in Belgium

routes.summary: Comoros authority-check route for family, study, research beyond short stay or longer stays where route-level public checklists are not stable.
routes.duration: Do not infer long-stay duration from a short-stay airport visa; confirm the stay basis with the competent authority.

source.label: Comoros embassy - visas
source.authority: Embassy of the Union of the Comoros in Belgium

routes.name: Work or Residence Authority Check
routes.summary: Comoros cautious work/residence check page for activity that may go beyond visitor, business or airport-visa permission.
routes.duration: Confirm the work or residence basis with the authority and employer; do not infer it from short-stay or business-visa handling.

source.label: Comoros embassy in Belgium
source.authority: Embassy of the Union of the Comoros in Belgium

routes.name: Visa Exemption Check
routes.summary: Kiribati visa-exemption route for travellers checking whether the 2023 exemption order removes the need for a pre-arranged visitor or transit visa.
routes.duration: Short-stay entry only; confirm the stay limit and conditions in the current exemption order or with Kiribati Immigration.

source.label: Kiribati Visa Exemption Order 2023
source.authority: Kiribati Immigration, Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Immigration

routes.name: Visitor Visa
routes.summary: Kiribati visitor visa route for tourists, family visitors, business visitors, guardians, dependent children and limited-purpose visits.
routes.duration: Temporary visitor stay; confirm the granted duration and any limited-purpose condition on the visa issued by Kiribati Immigration.

source.label: Kiribati Visitor Visa application form
source.authority: Kiribati Immigration, Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Immigration

routes.name: Group Visitor Visa
routes.summary: Kiribati group visitor handling where a tour organiser lodges a group form alongside individual visitor visa applications.
routes.duration: Same temporary visitor stay as the linked individual visitor applications; confirm the approved stay on each visa.

source.label: Kiribati Group Visitor Visa form
source.authority: Kiribati Immigration, Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Immigration

routes.name: Transit Visa
routes.summary: Kiribati transit visa route for travellers transiting through Kiribati who are not from a visa-waiver country.
routes.duration: Transit only; confirm the permitted transit time and conditions with Kiribati Immigration.

source.label: Kiribati Transit Visa application form
source.authority: Kiribati Immigration, Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Immigration

routes.name: Work Visa
routes.summary: Kiribati work visa route for Essential Skills, Specific Purpose or Event, Religious Worker and domestic worker categories.
routes.duration: Temporary work visa; confirm the granted work period and employer or purpose conditions on the visa.

source.label: Kiribati Work Visa application form
source.authority: Kiribati Immigration, Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Immigration

routes.name: Religious Worker Work Visa
routes.summary: Kiribati religious-worker work visa route for qualified religious workers sponsored by an eligible charitable religious organisation.
routes.duration: Temporary work visa; the religious-worker sponsorship form refers to support for one year from the first day as a Religious Worker work visa holder.

source.label: Kiribati Religious Worker sponsorship form
source.authority: Kiribati Immigration, Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Immigration

routes.name: Student Visa
routes.summary: Kiribati student visa route for temporary study in Kiribati with programme, funds, health and character evidence.
routes.duration: Temporary study stay tied to the approved programme dates; confirm the visa validity and any work or guardian condition on approval.

source.label: Kiribati Student Visa application form
source.authority: Kiribati Immigration, Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Immigration

routes.name: Investment Visa
routes.summary: Kiribati investment visa route for applicants with an approved Foreign Investment Certificate from the Investment Promotion Division.
routes.duration: Temporary investment-related stay; confirm the approved validity and any business conditions on the visa issued by Kiribati Immigration.

source.label: Kiribati Investment Visa application form
source.authority: Kiribati Immigration, Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Immigration

routes.name: Organised Tourism Authority Check

routes.name: Official, Diplomatic or Institutional Authority Check
routes.summary: North Korea authority-check route for diplomatic, official, institutional, delegation or mission-linked travel.

routes.summary: North Korea high-caveat authority-check route for work, study, residence, family, media, NGO or local-status cases.

routes.name: Residence permit for salaried workers
routes.summary: Luxembourg’s standard third-country employee route, usually starting with authorisation to stay before arrival.
routes.duration: First permit: normally up to 1 year, restricted to one profession and sector. Renewals can run for up to 3 years; exceptions apply.

source.label: Guichet.lu — Salaried third-country worker

routes.name: EU Blue Card
routes.summary: Luxembourg residence and work route for highly qualified third-country employees.
routes.duration: Time-limited permit; renewable under Luxembourg Blue Card rules.

source.label: Guichet.lu — EU Blue Card for highly qualified workers

routes.name: Residence permit for self-employed workers
routes.summary: Luxembourg route for third-country entrepreneurs and independent professionals whose activity benefits the country.
routes.duration: Up to 3 years for the first residence permit in many cases; renewable.

source.label: Guichet.lu — Self-employed third-country worker

routes.name: Residence Visa (Employment Category)
routes.summary: For you if a Sri Lankan employer or approved project needs your services: the employment-category residence visa lets foreign professionals live and work in Sri Lanka, usually a year at a time and renewable.
routes.duration: Generally issued for one year (or the period a competent authority recommends) and renewable annually.

source.label: Department of Immigration and Emigration - General Information on Visa
source.authority: Department of Immigration and Emigration (Sri Lanka)

routes.name: Digital Nomad Visa
routes.summary: For you if you work remotely for clients or a company based outside Sri Lanka: this brand-new visa (launched February 2026) lets you live in Sri Lanka while you keep earning from abroad.
routes.duration: Up to one year, renewable annually while you continue to meet the eligibility and compliance conditions; later renewals may require proof of Sri Lankan tax registration.

source.label: Department of Immigration and Emigration - Digital Nomad Visa Category
source.authority: Department of Immigration and Emigration (Sri Lanka)

routes.name: My Dream Home Visa Programme (retirement / long-stay residence)
routes.summary: For you if you are an older applicant who wants to retire or live long term in Sri Lanka: the My Dream Home programme grants a renewable residence visa to people who can support themselves from abroad.
routes.duration: Issued in two-year blocks and renewable while you continue to meet the conditions.

source.label: Department of Immigration and Emigration - My Dream Home Visa Programme
source.authority: Department of Immigration and Emigration (Sri Lanka)

routes.name: Residence Visa (Investor Category)
routes.summary: For you if you are putting capital into a business or venture in Sri Lanka: the investor-category residence visa lets you reside in the country while you set up and run your approved investment.
routes.duration: Tied to the approved investment; generally issued for a defined period and renewable while the investment and your involvement continue.

source.label: Department of Immigration and Emigration - General Information on Visa
source.authority: Department of Immigration and Emigration (Sri Lanka)

routes.name: Residence Visa (Approved-Project / BOI Professional)
routes.summary: For you if you are a professional whose services are needed on a government-approved or Board of Investment project: this residence visa lets you (and your dependents) live in Sri Lanka for the life of the project.
routes.duration: Generally tied to the project or the period recommended by a competent authority, and renewable while that continues.

source.label: Department of Immigration and Emigration - General Information on Visa
source.authority: Department of Immigration and Emigration (Sri Lanka)

routes.name: Visit Visa (Business Purpose)
routes.summary: For you if you are visiting Sri Lanka for short business activities like meetings or conferences: the business-purpose visit visa covers commercial trips - but it is not for taking up employment.
routes.duration: Short-stay visitor visa for the duration of the business trip; not a residence permit.

source.label: Department of Immigration and Emigration - General Information on Visa
source.authority: Department of Immigration and Emigration (Sri Lanka)

routes.name: Saint Lucia CBI - National Economic Fund
routes.summary: For people who want citizenship of Saint Lucia by making a one-time, non-refundable contribution to a national fund, rather than buying property or bonds. This is Saint Lucia's main donation route.
routes.duration: Full citizenship once the contribution is made and the application is approved.

source.label: Citizenship by Investment - CIP Saint Lucia
source.authority: Saint Lucia Citizenship by Investment Unit

routes.name: Saint Lucia CBI - Government Bonds
routes.summary: For people who want citizenship of Saint Lucia by buying government bonds that they hold for a fixed period - an option where the capital is intended to be returned at the end, unlike a donation.
routes.duration: Full citizenship; the bonds are held for a fixed period (historically five years) before the capital is returned.

source.label: Citizenship by Investment - CIP Saint Lucia
source.authority: Saint Lucia Citizenship by Investment Unit

routes.name: Saint Lucia CBI - Approved Real Estate
routes.summary: For people who would rather own an asset than donate: you buy into a government-approved property development in Saint Lucia and, in return, you and your family can apply for citizenship.
routes.duration: Full citizenship; the qualifying property must be held for a minimum period before it can be resold under the programme.

source.label: Citizenship by Investment - CIP Saint Lucia
source.authority: Saint Lucia Citizenship by Investment Unit

routes.name: Saint Lucia CBI - Enterprise Project
routes.summary: For investors who want citizenship of Saint Lucia by backing an approved enterprise project that creates local jobs - either alone or jointly with other approved applicants in a larger venture.
routes.duration: Full citizenship once the qualifying enterprise investment is made and the application is approved.

source.label: Citizenship by Investment - CIP Saint Lucia
source.authority: Saint Lucia Citizenship by Investment Unit

routes.name: Saint Lucia Work Permit
routes.summary: For people who have a job offer in Saint Lucia. Non-CARICOM nationals need a work permit from the Ministry of Labour before starting paid work; it is separate from citizenship by investment.
routes.duration: Typically a one-to-two-year, renewable permit tied to a specific employer; it does not by itself lead to citizenship.

source.label: Work Permit Unit (Labour Relations) - Government of Saint Lucia
source.authority: Ministry of Labour, Government of Saint Lucia

routes.name: Saint Lucia Permanent Residence
routes.summary: For people who want to settle long-term in Saint Lucia through the ordinary residence rules - typically after several years of continuous residence - rather than through investment.
routes.duration: Indefinite right to reside once granted; a separate work permit may still be needed to work.

source.label: Citizenship and Residency Services - Government of Saint Lucia

routes.name: Temporary Residence Permit for Employment (Lithuania)
routes.summary: If you have a Lithuanian job offer, this is the main route - a temporary residence permit for work, with a faster, quota-free lane for highly qualified roles.
routes.duration: Commonly issued for up to two years, and up to three years for highly qualified workers, renewable while you keep the job - confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: Migration Department - I am a highly skilled employee
source.authority: Migration Department under the Ministry of the Interior (Lithuania)

routes.name: EU Blue Card (Lithuania)
routes.summary: If you are a highly qualified professional with a Lithuanian job offer at the required salary, the EU Blue Card is a recognised route with EU-wide mobility.
routes.duration: Commonly issued for up to about three years where the contract allows, and renewable - confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: Migration Department - I am a highly skilled employee
source.authority: Migration Department under the Ministry of the Interior (Lithuania)

routes.name: Startup Visa (Lithuania)
routes.summary: If you are a non-EU founder with an innovative business idea, Lithuania's Startup Visa is a fast route to residence to build your company.
routes.duration: Commonly issued for one year first and extendable while the startup progresses - confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: Migration Department - Work and business in Lithuania
source.authority: Migration Department under the Ministry of the Interior (Lithuania)

routes.name: Temporary Residence for Business or Self-Employment (Lithuania)
routes.summary: If you set up or run your own company in Lithuania, this route gives you residence tied to that genuine business activity.
routes.duration: Commonly issued for up to two years and renewable while the business stays genuine and active - confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: Migration Department - Work and business in Lithuania
source.authority: Migration Department under the Ministry of the Interior (Lithuania)

routes.name: Temporary Residence for Family Reunification (Lithuania)
routes.summary: If a close family member lives lawfully in Lithuania, this route lets you join them and build toward settlement together.
routes.duration: Generally aligned to the sponsor's permit and renewable - confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: Migration Department - Work and business in Lithuania
source.authority: Migration Department under the Ministry of the Interior (Lithuania)

routes.name: Temporary Residence for Study (Lithuania)
routes.summary: If you have been admitted to a Lithuanian university or college, this residence permit lets you live in Lithuania for the length of your studies.
routes.duration: Tied to your course and renewable while you stay enrolled - confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: Migration Department - Work and business in Lithuania
source.authority: Migration Department under the Ministry of the Interior (Lithuania)

routes.name: Permanent Residence / EU Long-Term Resident Status (Lithuania)
routes.summary: If you have lived in Lithuania lawfully for five years, this is your settlement status - EU long-term resident rights and a stepping stone toward citizenship.
routes.duration: Longer-term status, subject to conditions on continued residence - confirm current rules on the official page.

routes.name: Temporary Residence Permit for Employment (Latvia)
routes.summary: If you have a Latvian job offer, this is the main route - a temporary residence permit tied to your employment with a Latvian employer.

source.label: PMLP - Residence permit
source.authority: Office of Citizenship and Migration Affairs (PMLP/OCMA), Latvia

routes.name: EU Blue Card (Latvia)
routes.summary: If you are a highly qualified professional with a Latvian job offer at the required salary, the EU Blue Card gives you residence with EU-wide mobility.
routes.duration: Tied to the contract and renewable while you keep qualifying employment - confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: PMLP - Residence permit
source.authority: Office of Citizenship and Migration Affairs (PMLP/OCMA), Latvia

routes.name: Startup Residence Permit (Latvia)
routes.summary: If you are a non-EU founder building an innovative product, Latvia's startup residence route lets you live there while you develop the business.
routes.duration: Commonly issued for an initial period and extendable while you actively develop the product - confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: PMLP - Innovative product creation or development (start-up activities)
source.authority: Office of Citizenship and Migration Affairs (PMLP/OCMA), Latvia

routes.name: Investor Residence Permit / Golden Visa (Latvia)
routes.summary: If you make a qualifying investment in Latvia - in a company, real estate, a bank deposit or government bonds - this route grants temporary residence.
routes.duration: Tied to maintaining the qualifying investment and renewable - confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: PMLP - Investments (investor residence)
source.authority: Office of Citizenship and Migration Affairs (PMLP/OCMA), Latvia

routes.name: Digital Nomad Visa (Latvia)
routes.summary: If you work remotely for an employer or your own business in an OECD country, this long-stay visa lets you live in Latvia while you keep earning from abroad.
routes.duration: Issued for up to one year and renewable once for a further year - confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: PMLP - Obtaining a long-stay visa for remote work
source.authority: Office of Citizenship and Migration Affairs (PMLP/OCMA), Latvia

routes.name: Residence Permit for Family Reunification (Latvia)
routes.summary: If a close family member lives lawfully in Latvia, this route lets you join them and build toward settlement together.
routes.duration: Generally aligned to the sponsor's permit and renewable - confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: PMLP - Residence permit
source.authority: Office of Citizenship and Migration Affairs (PMLP/OCMA), Latvia

routes.name: Temporary Residence for Study (Latvia)
routes.summary: If you have been admitted to a Latvian university or college, this residence permit lets you live in Latvia for the length of your studies.
routes.duration: Tied to your course and renewable while you stay enrolled - confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: PMLP - Residence permit
source.authority: Office of Citizenship and Migration Affairs (PMLP/OCMA), Latvia

routes.name: Permanent Residence / EU Long-Term Resident Status (Latvia)
routes.summary: If you have lived in Latvia lawfully for five years, this is your settlement status - EU long-term resident rights and a step toward citizenship.
routes.duration: Longer-term status, subject to conditions on continued residence - confirm current rules on the official page.

source.label: PMLP - Residence permit
source.authority: Office of Citizenship and Migration Affairs (PMLP/OCMA), Latvia

routes.name: Residence Permit B for Gainful Employment (Liechtenstein)
routes.summary: Residence Permit B is the residence branch for people who will live in Liechtenstein and have qualifying employment. Daily-return plans use a separate commuter classification.
routes.duration: Commonly issued for an initial period and renewable while you keep qualifying; the annual quota is very small - confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: Migration and Passport Office - Issue of residence permit (B) for employment
source.authority: Migration and Passport Office (Auslander- und Passamt), Liechtenstein

routes.name: Residence Permit B without Gainful Employment (Liechtenstein)
routes.summary: If you are an economically inactive EEA national who can support yourself, this lets you live in Liechtenstein - but, like the work permit, it is rationed and half is decided by lottery.
routes.duration: Commonly issued for an initial period and renewable while you keep qualifying; the annual quota is very small - confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: Migration and Passport Office - Residence permit draw (B) without gainful employment
source.authority: Migration and Passport Office (Auslander- und Passamt), Liechtenstein

routes.name: Cross-Border Commuter Permit / Grenzganger (Liechtenstein)
routes.summary: If you live in Austria or Switzerland and work in Liechtenstein, this is the realistic mass route - you work in Liechtenstein but return home, without using up a residence permit.
routes.duration: For EEA nationals, commonly valid for the term of the contract up to a set maximum and renewable; third-country commuters have stricter conditions - confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: Migration and Passport Office - Cross-border commuter permit (G) for third-country nationals
source.authority: Migration and Passport Office (Auslander- und Passamt), Liechtenstein

routes.name: Settlement Permit C (Liechtenstein)
routes.summary: If you have lived in Liechtenstein on a Permit B for around five years, this is your settlement status - more secure, longer-term residence.
routes.duration: Longer-term settlement status with fewer conditions than Permit B, subject to continued residence - confirm current rules on the official page.

source.label: Migration and Passport Office - Permanent residence and establishment
source.authority: Migration and Passport Office (Auslander- und Passamt), Liechtenstein

routes.name: Family Reunification (Liechtenstein)
routes.summary: If a close family member holds a Liechtenstein residence permit or is a citizen, this route lets you join them - though the same tight quota system shapes the timing.
routes.duration: Generally aligned to the sponsor's permit and renewable - confirm current validity on the official page.

source.label: Migration and Passport Office - Residence permits
source.authority: Migration and Passport Office (Auslander- und Passamt), Liechtenstein

source.authority: General Directorate of General Security, Republic of Lebanon

routes.name: Foreign Expert Port Visa

routes.summary: Residence visa for partners (married, civil union, or de facto) of New Zealand citizens or residents.

routes.name: Active Investor Plus Visa
routes.summary: Residence visa for investors committing at least NZD 5 million in the Growth category or NZD 10 million in the Balanced category.

routes.summary: Norway's main work permit for skilled workers requires a concrete job offer, relevant qualifications, normally full-time work (at least 80% can be accepted), and pay that meets UDI's normal-pay rules. It can lead to permanent residence after 3 years.

source.label: UDI — Skilled workers

routes.name: Job-Seeker Visa (Oppholdstillatelse for aa soeke arbeid som faglart)
routes.summary: Up to 1-year residence permit to enter Norway and search for skilled employment in person — available to qualified professionals.

source.label: UDI — Skilled workers seeking employment

routes.name: International Company Assignment Permit
routes.summary: Residence permit for skilled workers employed abroad who are assigned to a Norwegian branch or Norwegian client company.

source.label: UDI — Skilled workers: international company assignments

routes.name: Student Residence Permit (Oppholdstillatelse for studier)
routes.summary: Residence permit for international students at Norwegian universities — tuition-free at public institutions, with part-time work rights.
